articles.title: In 2017, nobody imagined a 22-year-old backup would become the face of the NFL; 9 years later, the league is quietly calculating how many more Super Bowls his arm has left in it
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes was a 22-year-old rookie sitting behind Alex Smith when the Kansas City Chiefs wrapped up the 2017 season.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes was a 22-year-old rookie sitting behind Alex Smith when the Kansas City Chiefs wrapped up the 2017 season. Nine years later, he is 31, owns three Super Bowl rings and has returned from a torn ACL and LCL. The Chiefs are 4-0 with him under center, and a contract through 2033 ties him to Kansas City. That raises a fair question about the rest of his career: how many more titles can he win? The answer depends less on his arm than on his knee, his offensive line and the roster around him.How a 22-year-old backup became the face of the NFLNobody in Kansas City planned a quick handoff. The Chiefs moved from the 27th pick to the 10th in 2017, sending Buffalo a third-round pick and their 2018 first-rounder along with it. Alex Smith, weeks from turning 33, was the starter. Mahomes was there to learn.He got one start that year. In the 2017 finale against Denver, he completed 22 of 35 passes for 284 yards with one interception in a 27-24 win. Broncos cornerback Aqib Talib walked away predicting Smith would hit free agency. Soon after, the Chiefs traded Smith to Washington for cornerback Kendall Fuller and a third-round pick, and the job was Mahomes' to keep.He kept it fast. In 2018 he threw for 5,097 yards and 50 touchdowns with only 12 interceptions. Five Super Bowl trips followed, three ending in wins and two in losses. That résumé is why one awkward step on a knee now moves the entire league.How did Patrick Mahomes come back from a torn ACL so fast?The knee gave out on December 14, 2025, in a 16-13 loss to the Chargers. Mahomes rolled to his right, threw the ball away and went down awkwardly. The diagnosis was a torn ACL and a torn LCL, and Dr. Dan Cooper operated in Dallas the next night. Kansas City finished 6-11, which meant a first missed postseason and a first losing season for Mahomes as a starter. Before the injury he had thrown for 3,587 yards with 22 touchdowns and 11 interceptions over 14 games.Most players need six to 12 months to return. Mahomes was back for the opener on September 14, exactly nine months after the injury, though the start was shaky. He finished 15 of 27 for 184 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, but he went 11 of 13 once he settled in, and the Chiefs won 31-10. Since then, Kansas City beat the Colts 33-30 in overtime, beat Miami 24-10 and edged the Raiders 30-27. Describing the Raiders game, Mahomes said, "I think you have to stay with it."Kenneth Walker III has helped. His 60-yard touchdown in the opener came in the best rushing game by a Chiefs running back in 14 years, and a steady ground game takes weight off Mahomes' arm and knee.Can Mahomes follow Tom Brady's path after a torn ACL?The comparison started the day he got hurt. Analyst Trey Wingo pointed out that Brady and Mahomes both won three Super Bowls early, then tore an ACL in their ninth seasons with their teams missing the playoffs. Brady tore the ACL and MCL in the 2008 opener and went on to win four more titles.The part people skip is the waiting. Brady's next ring came in the 2014 season, six years after the surgery, and his last arrived when he was 43. Along the way his roster kept changing, and so did the way he played. Mahomes is 31 now. The scrambler of 2018 will slow down like every quarterback does, so the real test is whether he can win more with his reads than with his legs.Joe Burrow tore his ACL and MCL in November 2020 and was back the next season, when he won Comeback Player of the Year. Daniel Jones tore his ACL in November 2023 and started Week 1 the following year. Mahomes fits that pattern.How many more Super Bowls can Mahomes win?Start with the calendar. His June extension runs through 2033, when he would be 38. The new money kicks in during 2027 at roughly $64 million a year, the richest average salary in the NFL, and he earns $56.8 million this season. Counting 2026, that is eight seasons of Chiefs football.Now the arithmetic. Mahomes is in his ninth year as the starter, and he won three titles in the first eight, about one every 2.7 years. Stretch that pace across the next eight and you land near three more. That is too generous. Age, injuries and the salary cap rarely allow straight lines. A smarter estimate is one or two more, and either would matter. One would tie him with Joe Montana and Terry Bradshaw at four. Two would put him at five, still well behind Brady's seven.Last year shows how thin the margin is. The Chiefs went 10-0 in one-score games in 2024 and 1-9 in 2025. Same core group, wildly different results.Who is protecting Mahomes this time?Protection is partly about targets who get open fast. Rashee Rice caught a 13-yard touchdown before halftime in the opener, and Tyquan Thornton added an eight-yard score in Las Vegas. Travis Kelce, in his 14th season, caught an 11-yard touchdown against Miami.The line is the bigger worry. Mahomes took heavy punishment behind an overwhelmed group last season, and the Chiefs benched a left guard during the Raiders game. Better protection matters more than any single throw, because it shortens the list of hits a repaired knee must absorb.The Chiefs had a backup plan. Andy Reid said in June that the team was ready to start Justin Fields in Week 1 if Mahomes was not. His own habits help. Chiefs sports medicine chief Rick Burkholder said Mahomes' structured lifestyle could speed his recovery, and the quarterback said in July that starting the opener was his goal. He made it.The next test comes Sunday, when the Chargers visit Kansas City. articles.title: "I just need to be the best dad that I can be”: Josh Allen opens up about life as a new dad alongside Hailee Steinfeld
articles.summary: Josh Allen, the Buffalo Bills’ quarterback, has remained strong on the field in the new season as his wife, Hailee Steinfeld, has shown up for him, just
articles.body: Josh Allen, the Buffalo Bills’ quarterback, has remained strong on the field in the new season as his wife, Hailee Steinfeld, has shown up for him, just months after giving birth to their daughter, Harper. While Hailee Steinfeld has been public about how her life changed when she gave birth, the Buffalo Bills’ quarterback Josh Allen has also opened up about the changes as he became a father.Josh Allen reflects on the changes he had to adjust to as a father as he remains unbeatable on the fieldA few weeks ago, in an interview with The Healthy, the popular quarterback Josh Allen reflected on his sleep pattern as he said, “I think young me would say that getting to bed before midnight was a win, and now it’s like, if I’m not in bed by 9:15, we got a problem. Because, as you know, that baby’s not going to wait until you’re rested. They’re getting up when they want to get up, and if you’re not rested and recovered, that’s on you, right?”The 4 time Pro Bowler added, “That’s on me—that’s my fault. So I just need to be the best dad that I can be. That’s all I’m focused on right now—making sure that I can get as much sleep as possible and just be as present and as good of a dad as I can be right now.”Josh Allen continued, “But it’s the whole regimen, if you will—waking up, making sure I can work out, making sure I’m doing everything I need to be doing for the football side of it, but also being the best dad that I can be, and as helpful as I can be.”He added, “So, sometimes it’s the 2 to 5 a.m. shift, right? If the baby’s up, I’m up, too, that’s just what it is. And sometimes it’s making sure I’m changing an extra diaper, whatever it is.”Josh Allen and his wife, Hailee Steinfeld, remain private about their daughter as he focuses on the new seasonBoth Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld have remained pretty public about their marriage and even their relationship. But it seems, the moment they became parents to their daughter, Harper, both of them became more and more private about their lives.While Josh Allen and the BAFTA nominated actress Hailee Steinfeld have revealed their daughter’s name, they have stayed away from sharing any pictures of her.For now, all eyes remain on Josh Allen’s performance as most recently, he carried the Buffalo Bills to a 37-34 overtime win against the Los Angeles Rams, securing his first ever career overtime victory that included 210 passing yards, 121 rushing yards, and two total touchdowns.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “God has put me in this position to overcome it”: Dak Prescott leans on his faith as the Dallas Cowboys navigate a difficult start to the season
articles.summary: Dak Prescott, the Dallas Cowboys’ star player and popular quarterback, saw his wedding to ex fiance, Sarah Jane Ramos, being called off at the last moment
articles.body: Dak Prescott, the Dallas Cowboys’ star player and popular quarterback, saw his wedding to ex fiance, Sarah Jane Ramos, being called off at the last moment during the offseason as the team struggles in the new season. The Dallas Cowboys have recently lost against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5 and it has sparked major concern. Amid this, Dak Prescott has reflected on his faith.Dak Prescott opens up about how God played an important role in his life and helped him to recover as the Dallas Cowboys struggleIn an interview post match, the popular quarterback of the Dallas Cowboys, Dak Prescott said, “I’ve been through so much in my life. God’s always been the reason and, yeah, who I fall back on and my refuge, as I say…”The star player added, “I can’t thank Him enough and never will be able to thank Him enough and just to see that transcend throughout our team, starting with our head coach, is special. It’s something that we take pride in.”The Dallas Cowboys’ star player continued, “At the end of the day, it’s about giving Him the glory,” Prescott asserted. “From that, good things will come. All great things will come. And so, I’m thankful for that. Even sitting there, holding my leg or whatever on the field, trying to put it back into place, or later on being in the hospital and waking up from surgery, that’s just what God’s thrown at me…”The 4 time Pro Bowler said, “If you’ve known my life, if you’ve known my story, whatever circumstance that is, I’m going to take it with a smile and be thankful that God has put me in this position to overcome it, to be an example to others. Through this whole time, I never had any doubt in my mind that I wouldn’t be here,” he continued, characterizing himself as “a guy that lives and stands and moves every part of his body off the word ‘faith.’”Dak Prescott remains a reliable quarterback amid drama in his personal lifeIn the 2026 NFL season, Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott has carried a heavy workload through five games, throwing for 1,381 passing yards, 9 touchdowns, and 3 interceptions. While maintaining a solid 67.2% completion percentage and a 97.2 passer rating, the Dallas Cowboys have struggled on the field due to a struggling defensive unit.Amid this, the star player has also been struggling with a lot of drama in his personal life as the cheating rumors concerning his relationship have refused to die down.For now, Dak Prescott and Sarah Jane Ramos are co-parenting their two daughters as they navigate through a tough break up.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “The divorce was very upsetting, but she’s not bitter”: Gisele Bündchen opens up about Tom Brady divorce, revealing why she feels grateful despite the pain
articles.summary: Gisele Bündchen once believed she would spend the rest of her life married to Tom Brady.
articles.body: Gisele Bündchen once believed she would spend the rest of her life married to Tom Brady. Their divorce in October 2022 brought an end to 13 years of marriage, leaving her struggling to understand how their relationship had reached that point. But the Brazilian model has no lingering bitterness toward the former NFL quarterback, according to a source close to her who spoke to PEOPLE. She is now grateful for the years they shared and the family they built, while embracing a new chapter with her husband, Joaquim Valente, and their growing family in Miami.Gisele Bündchen is grateful for her years with Tom Brady despite their painful divorce“She always thought she would be married to Tom for the rest of her life,” the source told PEOPLE. “The divorce was very upsetting, and she struggled to understand it at the time, but she’s not bitter.”That distinction offers a glimpse into how Bündchen views the end of their marriage today. The separation was difficult, but it has not erased the value she places on their life together. The source said she remains “grateful for their children and the years they shared.”Brady and Bündchen have two children together, son Benjamin, 16, and daughter Vivian, 13. Bündchen has also spoken publicly about wanting the best for Brady, even after their relationship ended.In a 2023 Vanity Fair cover interview, she pushed back against reports that their split came down to an ultimatum over Brady's football career. She called those claims “very hurtful” and “the craziest thing I’ve ever heard.”“What’s been said is one piece of a much bigger puzzle. It’s not so black and white,” she said, acknowledging how painful it was to see the end of their marriage reduced to a single explanation.She also made her feelings toward Brady clear. “Listen, I have always cheered for [Tom], and I would continue forever… If there’s one person I want to be the happiest in the world, it’s him, believe me. I want him to achieve and to conquer. I want all his dreams to come true. That’s what I want, really, from the bottom of my heart.”A new family life with Joaquim ValenteBündchen's life has changed considerably since the divorce. She married jiu-jitsu instructor Joaquim Valente in December 2025. The couple welcomed a son in February 2025, though Bündchen has not publicly revealed his name.“She feels so blessed to have become a mom again,” the source told PEOPLE. “She loves the life she has with Joaquim and their family in Miami.”The source also described Bündchen as spiritual, saying she now believes “the universe had another plan for her.” Her new marriage appears to have brought happiness without requiring her to dismiss what came before.A source told PEOPLE in March that Bündchen was “really happy” with Valente. Their marriage, the insider said, had not dramatically changed their daily routine, but had made their relationship feel more meaningful.The latest comments come after the September 29 release of Lars Anderson's book, Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness. The book revisits the breakdown of Brady and Bündchen's marriage, including Brady's reported request for an extended leave from Tampa Bay Buccaneers training camp in the summer of 2022 so the couple could work on their relationship privately in the Bahamas.Brady and Bündchen finalized their divorce on October 28, 2022, ending a 13-year marriage. The relationship did not end as Bündchen had hoped, but her reported comments suggest she is no longer measuring her life by that outcome. She has a new family, a different marriage and two children whose parents will remain connected long after their divorce.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' 15 and the Mahomies Foundation has a meaningful mission for young people
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes set up 15 and the Mahomies Foundation in 2019 with one clear aim: to improve the lives of children.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes set up 15 and the Mahomies Foundation in 2019 with one clear aim: to improve the lives of children. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback pointed the charity at health, wellness and communities that lack resources. Its signature program, 15 for 15, backs 15 youth initiatives covering school, science, the arts, sports and after-school care. The name carries his jersey number, and the number shows up everywhere in how the foundation works. Seven years on, the mission still centers on giving kids chances they might not get otherwise, on the field and far from it.What is the mission behind 15 and the Mahomies?The foundation says it exists to improve children's lives. That sounds broad, and it is meant to be. Support goes toward health and wellness projects, classroom needs, and communities short on resources.Executive Director Marques Fitch has explained the focus in plain terms. "We focus on education, we focus on athletics," Fitch said. He then added the arts and the unique experiences many children would never get to try. He also says the team keeps stressing the good sports can do in a child's life.The 15 for 15 model makes it concrete. Each initiative helps 15 people or 15 organizations. The first sponsored 15 athletes in the Special Olympics. Year-round entry costs $460 per athlete, so those athletes did not have to worry about the fee.Another 2019 effort sent 15 kids from the Boys & Girls Club of Lubbock to Texas Tech home games. Mahomes played college ball there. "Providing memorable experiences for deserving kids is a big part of our mission," he said.Fans can join in too. When the foundation launched, the suggested donation was $15, which kept the theme intact.How do Read for 15 and Volunteer for 15 work?Read for 15 is a virtual, 15-week program. Children, classrooms and parents take a pledge to read for 15 minutes a day outside school. Parents get a role too, which matters for a habit that has to survive a busy weeknight. The foundation also provides management support for Read for 15 in Kansas City schools. The aim is simple: more kids who love books and do well in class.Volunteer for 15 flips the script. Here, young people are the helpers. The foundation teams up with Youth Volunteer Corps, and kids aged 11 to 18 commit 15 hours of service. The foundation says that teaches respect, kindness and leadership, along with a better understanding of people who are different.Put together, the programs cover a child's week. Reading builds a habit at home. Service builds one in the community. The 15 for 15 initiatives add the experiences in between, like a seat at a college football game.The reach goes beyond Kansas City. In Whitehouse, Texas, the foundation has donated shoes to students in the district where Mahomes grew up. "Whitehouse will always have a special place in Patrick's heart," Fitch said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $200 million investment hit with another lawsuit as Six Flags River injury claims emerge
articles.summary: Travis Kelce’s connection to Six Flags is drawing fresh attention as a fatal roller coaster incident in Georgia raises questions about theme park safety.
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s connection to Six Flags is drawing fresh attention as a fatal roller coaster incident in Georgia raises questions about theme park safety. The Kansas City Chiefs star has ties to the amusement park industry as an ambassador and investor in Six Flags, putting the company’s latest crisis under a brighter spotlight. While the investigation into the death at Six Flags Over Georgia continues, an earlier lawsuit involving a different ride at the same park has resurfaced. The case, filed by two guests over injuries allegedly sustained on a water raft attraction, adds another layer to the growing scrutiny surrounding the park.Six Flags Over Georgia faces renewed scrutiny after fatal Goliath incidentHassan Jihad Ibn Kariem died Monday after being thrown from Goliath, a roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia that reportedly reaches speeds close to 70 mph. Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the fatal incident, and the ride has been shut down while they work to establish what happened.The death has raised serious questions about ride safety and the measures theme parks take to protect visitors. Investigators will need to determine how the incident occurred before drawing conclusions about responsibility.For Kelce, whose public profile extends beyond football through business partnerships and investments, the situation brings additional attention to his association with Six Flags. However, there is no indication that the Chiefs tight end had any involvement in the ride’s operation or the circumstances surrounding the death.The distinction matters as the investigation develops. A business association alone does not establish responsibility for an incident at an individual park.Previous Six Flags lawsuit involved Thunder River water raft rideThe latest incident has also brought renewed attention to a lawsuit filed against Six Flags Over Georgia in 2024 by Bryce and Beatrice Jamison.According to TMZ, the couple alleged that Bryce suffered injuries while riding Thunder River during a visit to the park in July 2022. Their complaint claimed that the raft struck part of the ride’s terrain, throwing him from his seat despite his belief that he had secured his seatbelt.Bryce alleged that the belt appeared to be latched when it was not, leaving him vulnerable when the raft collided with the terrain. He claimed the incident injured his arm, neck, shoulder, back and thigh.The couple sued the company, alleging negligence and seeking damages that included loss of consortium, a claim related to the impact of an injury on a spouse.However, the case did not proceed to a trial. The Jamisons voluntarily dismissed their lawsuit, and the dismissal was with prejudice, meaning they cannot file the same claim again. It remains unclear whether the parties reached a settlement.TMZ reported that it contacted Six Flags for comment on the earlier lawsuit but had not received a response at the time of publication.The two incidents involve separate rides and different circumstances. The earlier allegations do not establish the cause of the fatal Goliath incident, which remains under investigation. As authorities examine the latest tragedy, the focus will remain on determining what happened and whether any safety failures contributed to the death.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Josh Allen delivered a performance to remember against the Los Angeles Rams, but a bold comparison from Jason Whitlock has given Buffalo Bills fans
articles.body: Josh Allen delivered a performance to remember against the Los Angeles Rams, but a bold comparison from Jason Whitlock has given Buffalo Bills fans something else to debate. After Allen powered his team to a dramatic 37-34 overtime win, Whitlock compared the quarterback to O.J. Simpson, the former Bills running back. The remark quickly became a talking point, with fans weighing in on Allen’s rushing ability, his place in Buffalo history and the criticism surrounding his performances. While some celebrated the comparison, others were far less comfortable with it.Jason Whitlock compares Josh Allen to O.J. Simpson after Bills winAllen put on a show on Monday night, rushing 10 times for 121 yards and a touchdown while completing 12 of 19 passes for 210 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Tyler Bass sealed the victory with a 45-yard field goal in overtime, lifting Buffalo to a 4-1 record.Whitlock shared his verdict on X, writing, “Josh Allen is OJ Simpson in a Bills uniform.”He later defended his argument by pointing to Allen’s size and running power.“I guess when you’re 6-foot-5, 240 pounds, the rules don’t apply, and he can still run the football like O.J. Simpson,” Whitlock said.Whitlock also made an MVP case for Allen, citing his contribution to Buffalo’s offence despite the defence allowing 34 points against the Rams.“If that’s not the MVP, I don’t know who is,” Whitlock said.However, the comparison sparked mixed reactions among fans, who had plenty to say about Allen’s performance and the reference to Simpson.Josh Allen comparison divides Bills fans on social mediaSome fans focused on Allen’s place in Bills history, while others questioned whether the quarterback deserved such praise.One fan highlighted Allen’s rushing achievements, writing, “Josh passed OJ in rushing touchdowns but is still 2 behind OJ on the all time murders list.”Another wrote, "oo sh*t, pray for Hailee Steinfeld then."Another user recalled Simpson’s playing days against New England, saying, “Didn’t OJ play for the Bills? I remember he used to run all over my Patriots.”Allen’s critics also joined the discussion. One commenter pointed to his turnovers, writing, “4 picks in 5 games... he on pace to throw 13-14 this season please shu... Brock is blowing this guy out the water rn”Another fan argued that Allen could improve his decision-making, saying, “They would win more if he could learn to utilize the pocket. Get under center. Freeze the linebackers....”Others pushed back against comparisons involving Simpson. One fan wrote, “Josh won’t be cutting her head off anytime soon, that’s an insult”A separate commenter made their position clear: “Don’t ever compare Our Josh Allen to That man!”Meanwhile, another fan praised the original post, writing, “This may be the greatest tweet of all time about Josh Allen. 🔥🔥🔥 👏🏻👏🏻”One user defended Allen despite concerns about his supporting cast, saying, “Imagine if Allen actually had a receiver that could get separation. Not a Bills fan but how can you not be an Allen fan.”Another fan shared a more straightforward reaction to watching Allen play: “Hell yea... the juice was amazing got to see him play! Great take.....”The debate highlights the strong emotions surrounding Allen, whose explosive running helped Buffalo survive a high-scoring contest. Yet the comparison with Simpson has ensured that the conversation extends well beyond the final score.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "I wish...": Patrick Mahomes’ mom Randi Mahomes breaks silence on claims that Chiefs star owns a Lake of the Ozarks home
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to headlines, but not every story about the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback comes with a factual basis.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to headlines, but not every story about the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback comes with a factual basis. A rumour claiming the NFL star owns a home at Lake of the Ozarks has circulated across social media, leaving fans to wonder whether he has a private lakeside retreat. Now, his mother, Randi Mahomes, has stepped in to set the record straight. Her response was brief, but it offered a clear answer to a story that has continued to resurface online despite a lack of confirmation.Randi Mahomes responds to Patrick Mahomes’ Lake of the Ozarks home rumourThe latest round of speculation began after a video circulated on Instagram claiming that Mahomes owned a property at Lake of the Ozarks in Missouri. The post gained attention as users shared the possibility of the Chiefs star enjoying time away from football at a luxurious lakeside home.However, the person behind the post later acknowledged the information was unreliable. An update added to the video read: "Sources are incorrect."Randi Mahomes also came across the claim and responded directly in the comments. Rather than issuing a lengthy statement, she offered a short reaction that made her position clear."I wish," Randi Mahomes wrote in the comments, "i love the lake"Her remark suggested that she would welcome the idea of a family home by the water, but it did not confirm that her son owned one. The response also brought a little humour to a rumour that had travelled across several social media platforms.According to The Kansas City Star, the claim had appeared on Reddit, Facebook, YouTube and Instagram. Its repeated circulation shows how quickly unverified stories about high-profile athletes can gain traction online.Travis Kelce previously called out fake AI-generated storyMahomes is not the only Chiefs star whose name has been attached to questionable online claims. His teammate Travis Kelce previously addressed an AI-generated story alleging that he had purchased a $3.3 million home in Kansas City to help homeless young people.The story attracted attention because it portrayed Kelce as making a major charitable contribution. However, the tight end publicly denied the claim and urged fans to be more careful about what they believe online."I gotta make a little statement in the 'don't believe everything you read, kids' category or nice realm that you see online," Kelce said.He also directed people towards his foundation's website, 87running.org, for accurate information about his community work.The false reports have highlighted a growing problem for athletes whose personal lives attract constant attention. AI-generated content, misleading captions and repeated social media posts can make unsupported claims appear credible.For now, there is no confirmation that Mahomes owns a home at Lake of the Ozarks. Randi's response has put the rumour back in the spotlight, but the quarterback's supposed lakeside property remains an unverified claim rather than an established fact.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NFL Catchup: Saquon Barkley Among 24 Eagles On Injury Report; Caleb Williams Returns
articles.summary: Here’s the latest from around the NFL on Wednesday.
articles.body: Wednesday in the NFL brought updates on two quarterbacks working their way back from injury. The Baltimore Ravens and Chicago Bears provided updates on their situations ahead of the weekend. Lamar Jackson is inching closer to a return for the Ravens, while Caleb Williams took a real step forward in Chicago. Jackson was absent again from the portion of Ravens practice open to reporters, but there's a "realistic chance" he plays Sunday against the Cleveland Browns. Meanwhile, Williams was a full participant in the Bears’ Wednesday walkthrough, the clearest sign yet that he could be back under center against the Atlanta Falcons. Here’s the latest from around the NFL on Wednesday. Caleb Williams Returns To Practice Bears quarterback Caleb Williams took a real step toward returning for Sunday’s game against the Falcons, serving as a full participant in Chicago’s Wednesday walkthrough after missing the past three weeks with a hamstring injury. It’s a positive sign that Williams could be back on the field soon, but head coach Ben Johnson didn't rush to say his return would come against Atlanta when asked who would start under center this week. "It’s still fluid," Johnson told reporters, "but I feel good about the plan that we have in place at this point." Williams showed progress last week, logging a limited practice and working through pregame warm-ups as he inches closer to a return. The 2022 Heisman Trophy winner was initially expected to miss three to four games after injuring his hamstring in Week 2, and the Bears went 2-1 without him, with backups Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent each starting and picking up a win, though Bagent struggled in last week’s 31-7 loss to the Packers. Johnson also acknowledged the tight turnaround before Chicago’s Thursday night game against the Falcons could factor into how the team handles the quarterback's workload regardless of who starts. "I don't know that any of them are exactly 100% at this point of the season, so that's something that we certainly look at," Johnson said. Barkley, DeVonta Smith Still Out As Offense Struggles Running back Saquon Barkley and Wide Receiver DeVonta Smith both sat out again Wednesday as the Eagles opened their practice week ahead of Sunday’s game against the Panthers, both still nursing hamstring injuries. Barkley missed last week’s game in London after playing just four snaps against the Rams the week prior, and Smith has now missed the last two games. Philadelphia’s offense has cratered without its two biggest weapons as the Eagles have managed just 404 total yards over those two losses. Earlier in the week, head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters he was "hopeful" one or both could return this week. The need is especially urgent at running back, where backup Tank Bigsby is on injured reserve and third-stringer Will Shipley is now expected to miss multiple weeks with a foot injury suffered against the Jaguars. That left Philadelphia finishing that game with two practice-squad call-ups, Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele, and just 22 rushing yards on 18 carries — the team’s lowest rushing output in a game since 2015. Barkley and Smith are far from the only Eagles players dealing with injuries as six players sat out Wednesday’s practice in total, while 11 other players were limited participants. Seven more Eagles players were listed as full participants on Wednesday's injury report, including quarterback Jalen Hurts (calf). Lamar Jackson Absent At Practice Wednesday Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson was missing again from the open portion of Ravens' practice Wednesday as he continues working back from the ankle injury that’s already cost him one game. Ravens Head Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday that Jackson was "definitely day-to-day" adding, "To Lamar’s credit, he’s working his butt off and he's doing everything he can to be out here." ESPN reported Wednesday that Jackson has a "realistic chance" to play Sunday. Jackson went down two weeks ago in a win over the Titans, sacked on the final play of the first half with a sprained left ankle. He completed 15 of 20 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns before having to leave the game. Tyler Huntley has stepped in his place after filling in for Jackson nearly half of last season, throwing for 201 yards and two scores and rushing for the winning touchdown in overtime of last week’s win over the Falcons. At 4-1, Baltimore has some margin to be careful with Jackson’s return, especially after last season’s hamstring injury lingered well past his initial comeback. Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. isn't expected to be sidelined long after exiting late against the Baltimore Ravens with a rib injury. A.J. Brown Returns To Practice Since suffering a high-ankle sprain in Week 1, wide receiver A.J. Brown has been on injured reserve, but his return could take place as early as Sunday. Head coach Mike Vrabel announced Wednesday that Brown has been designated to return to practice. Brown returned to practice on Wednesday in a limited capacity as he works his way back to full strength. The Patriots acquired Brown from the Philadelphia Eagles this offseason for a 2028 first-round pick. The offense has had plenty of ups and downs since his injury, but both Romeo Doubs and Efton Chism III have seen steady improvements in production since. Getting Brown back into an improving offense will be huge for Drake Maye as the Patriots push to stay competitive in the AFC playoff picture. Penix Jr. Expected To Start Against Bears Head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters on Wednesday that Michael Penix Jr. is expected to start against the Chicago Bears, barring any setbacks. Since entering the league, he has struggled to stay healthy, so avoiding missed time is a positive sign for both Penix and the Falcons. Following Penix’s exit against the Ravens, backup quarterback Tua Tagovailoa came in and threw a game-ending interception in overtime. Before his injury, Penix was having a strong outing, throwing for 240 yards and a touchdown. Through his first three starts this season, Penix is off to the best stretch of his career, especially impressive considering he's returning from a season-ending knee injury. He's completed 67.5% of his passes for 719 yards, three touchdowns, and just one interception. Keeping Penix on the field is massive for a Falcons team competing in a wide-open NFC South. articles.title: Is Nick Sirianni getting too much hate? Michael Vick asks the Philadelphia Eagles fans to give their head coach more time
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles have lost three straight games, and head coach Nick Sirianni is facing growing criticism.
articles.body: The Philadelphia Eagles have lost three straight games, and head coach Nick Sirianni is facing growing criticism. Their latest defeat, a 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on October 11, 2026, left fans frustrated after Philadelphia gave up a late lead. However, former Eagles quarterback Michael Vick has a different view. He believes the team still has the right coach and quarterback combination, and he wants fans to stop turning on Sirianni so quickly.Vick spoke up as the Eagles entered Week 6 with a 2-3 record. Philadelphia has struggled to finish games, and its offense has failed to find the end zone after halftime since Week 2. Still, Vick believes the team needs patience rather than more pressure on its head coach. Michael Vick backs Nick Sirianni as Eagles fans question his futureVick did not hold back while defending Sirianni. In comments shared by BG Unblocked on X, the former Eagles quarterback urged fans to give the coach more time to get things right.“It’s just a couple more years, year to, it’ll start a trend back in the right direction,” Vick said. “And then they got the right coach too, man. Everybody need to get off Nick’s back, man.”He continued by defending the partnership between Sirianni and quarterback Jalen Hurts. Vick said, “I’m just saying, man, you got a good leader and a great coach and you got that tandem of head coach and quarterback. Leave it alone.”Vick also made it clear that he was not trying to disrespect Philadelphia fans. Instead, he wanted them to give the current leadership a chance to work through the rough patch.“I love, I ain’t gonna disrespect our Eagles fans, but I’m always telling the truth because they real. But let this combination ride out, baby. Don’t get too impatient right now,” he added.His defense comes after another painful finish for Philadelphia. The Eagles led Jacksonville 17-16 after Jake Elliott kicked a 48-yard field goal with eight seconds left on October 11. Yet Philadelphia chose to kick off rather than aim for a touchback. Ameer Abdullah returned the ball, giving Jacksonville an opportunity to respond. Cam Little then made a 57-yard field goal to seal the 19-17 win.Sirianni accepted responsibility for the decision after the game. “I didn’t make the right decision, and it cost us the game,” he said. “There’s no other way around it.”Why the Eagles need more than Nick Sirianni’s apologyAlthough Sirianni took the blame, Philadelphia's problems go beyond one late-game call. The offense struggled throughout the afternoon, and Saquon Barkley left with a hamstring injury that the team considered week-to-week. Dameon Pierce managed just 14 rushing yards on 11 carries.Hurts also had a difficult outing. He completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and one touchdown as Jacksonville repeatedly pressured him. The Eagles managed a late drive to set up Elliott’s field goal, but their defense and special teams could not protect the lead.The loss also marked Philadelphia’s second straight game in which it surrendered a fourth-quarter advantage, following its defeat to the Los Angeles Rams. According to ESPN analytics cited in the original report, the Eagles had more than a 98% chance of winning each game at one point.Former Eagles running back LeSean McCoy also pointed to the offense when discussing the team’s struggles. Speaking on his Speakeasy show with Emmanuel Acho, McCoy said, “First of all, I’m gonna blame the offense first, right? We can look at Nick Sirianni and blame this and blame that, but the truth is the offense did not play well. The defense played great!”Philadelphia now faces the Carolina Panthers before a meeting with the Dallas Cowboys. Vick wants fans to stay patient, but the Eagles must improve quickly. Sirianni has admitted his mistake. articles.title: Cleveland Browns News and Rumors 10/15/26: Have Your People Call My People
articles.summary: CLEVELAND, OHIO (TheOBR.com) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans!THE DAILY BLOVIATIONYesterday, I mentioned that I follow a list of articles from the 3,297...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND, OHIO ( TheOBR.com ) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans!

Yesterday, I mentioned that I follow a list of articles from the 3,297 or so aggregators that cover the Browns by recycling content from actual reporters and feeding off each other. I don't really read them, but I keep an eye on what they're up to, in case there's some gold to be panned from the resulting hundreds of articles competing for the attention of Browns fans. You never know; one of them may stumble across something significant. But generally, I just delete them each morning after giving them a cursory glance.

On the opposite end of the credibility spectrum, I keep a much closer eye on everyone you might expect, including the well-connected Adam Schefter.

Late Wednesday morning, Schefter posted a few dozen words : Shedeur Sanders, "who went through draft night and the early part of his NFL career without an agent," has signed with Adie von Gontard, CEO of Young Money APAA Sports. That's the same agency that represents his old Colorado teammate, Travis Hunter.

Everything after that was the internet trying to answer one question. "Why?" In the span of an afternoon, a man signing a piece of paper was described as "significant," "curious," a "career move," a reason for "analysts" to raise their eyebrows, and, my favorite, "officially on trade watch," a phrase one of them lifted from a Steelers fan account.

So since nobody actually knows, let's do what everybody else did and guess. Why did Shedeur Sanders hire an agent?

THEORY ONE, HE WANTS OUT: This is the one with the most smoke. Armando Salguero at OutKick (an outlet whose genesis was built on bashing my alma mater) says "multiple NFL sources" believe Sanders hired representation "because he's getting ready to press for a trade." Then, one sentence later: "none of the sources speaking about Sanders are directly tied to his family." I appreciate the honesty. That's a polite way of saying the sources are guessing too.

The precedent everybody cites is Marvin Harrison Jr., who went without an agent in Arizona, hired Tory Dandy and Todd France, and got shipped to Houston for a second and a seventh. When did he hire them? A national outlet says Oct. 9 . Pro Football Rumors says two weeks ago. One of the aggregators claims it was near the end of September. Three outlets, three dates. All three think they know where Shedeur is headed.

Salguero also adds Minkah Fitzpatrick, circa 2019, to the list of players who hired an agent to force a trade. Yes, that Minkah. The one who knocked KC Concepcion out cold on Sunday. Small league.

CBS has already drawn up the landing spots: Tampa Bay, Jacksonville (Hunter!), Denver (back to Colorado!), Miami and Dallas, where the reasoning is, and I quote, "you might as well include the Cowboys" because Deion played there. By that standard, the Cincinnati Reds should be making calls.

THEORY TWO, THE BROWNS TOLD HIM SOMETHING: Emmett Golden on ESPN Cleveland, via an aggregator: "Why would a guy need an agent all of a sudden? Either Shedeur went to the Browns and said I would prefer a trade...or the Browns sat Shedeur down and said, 'Hey listen, we're going to activate Dillon (Gabriel) in a couple of weeks, and we're going to release you unless we find a trade partner.'" The article quotes exactly one radio host. The headline says "Analysts." Plural.

Against that: PFT notes the Browns "have not shown an interest in moving Sanders," and Pro Football Rumors has reported the team is likely to keep four quarterbacks once Gabriel comes off IR. CBS, same day, says there's "no reason for the Browns to keep four quarterbacks." Pick your source. The beat writer's version turns up in a minute, in the last place you'd look.

THEORY THREE, HE'S FRUSTRATED: Another radio host, again on ESPN Cleveland: "Young buck wants to play ball. I have no problem with that. None. He's frustrated. I could argue he was done wrong here." One site put "He Was Done Wrong Here" in the headline. Through five games, Shedeur has had one pass attempt, a completion for zero yards. Of course he's frustrated. He's a backup quarterback. Frustration comes with the clipboard.

THEORY FOUR, THE INTERNET SAID SO: Another site went live with a collection of replies to Schefter's post, including "Steelers Black and Gold Nation" declaring Sanders "officially on trade watch" and "The AZ sports fan!" with "He saw Marvin Harrison Jr. do it, he obviously wants out of the Browns." It also quotes its own account, which posted "Shedeur tryna get traded?" along with the eyeballs emoji. A website quoting its own tweet in a story about what people are tweeting. Somebody has finally built a perpetual motion machine, and it runs on clicks.

A few paragraphs further down, that same piece mentions Mary Kay Cabot's Sept. 27 report that the Browns had no plans to trade Sanders or Gabriel and were "happy to have Sanders as their No. 2." It's in there. You just have to get past the Steelers fans.

While we're mucking around: One site credits Watson's early success to "Stefanski's offense," which will come as news to Todd Monken. It also suggests "Texas" might explore getting draft capital for one of its quarterbacks, and it mentions a "20027 second-round pick," which is a long time to wait on a pick.

THEORY FIVE, HE JUST WANTED AN AGENT: At least one site said out loud that it's "at least equally plausible that Sanders just decided to hire an agent at this time and chose the same one as his buddy." Another makes some noise about marketing. And CBS's John Breech kills the money theory: a 2025 draftee can't negotiate a new deal until after the 2027 season. Shedeur's rookie contract is four years, $4.647 million, and runs through 2028, per NFL Trade Rumors . Nobody is renegotiating anything this month.

MY THEORY: This is worth exactly what you paid for it. Which, by happenstance, is about $7 less than a Pumpkin Squeeze Maple Iced Machiatto or whatever.

Shedeur tried it the other way. He went through the 2025 draft with no agent and his inner circle running the show. His dad called the pre-draft criticism "bull junk." A quarterback who'd been mocked in the first round went 144th overall. Bleacher Report put it gently: he "didn't have an advocate who could push back."

Now he's 24, backing up a 31-year-old in the last year of a contract nobody wants, and ESPN's Dan Graziano just wrote that "it would be stunning if the Browns' 2027 starter is someone on the current roster." Shedeur can read too.

So he hired a professional. It's the most conventional thing he's done since he got to Cleveland, and probably the smartest. Good for him.

Does he want to know if anybody out there wants him? Sure. That's what you'd ask an agent to find out in the middle of October, with the deadline on Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. Salguero has that part right: rather than fight it himself, a player can "grit his teeth, stay quiet and hire an agent to do something on his behalf."

Does that mean he gets traded? Different question. Pro Football Rumors calls his trade value "not too high presently." In our own Watercooler thread , Iko got it down to four words: "He has zero leverage."

The Browns have a cheap quarterback under contract through 2028 in a league where quarterbacks get hurt every Sunday. CBS's own list includes Tampa Bay, where Baker Mayfield's thumb has an undrafted rookie named Jalen Daniels starting. Andrew Berry isn't giving away a cheap QB in October because an agent called. If somebody calls with a real pick, that's a different conversation. I have faith he knows the difference.

None of the stories I read Wednesday had a single word from Shedeur himself.

Which, for the record, is exactly what you pay an agent for.

BEFORE I TAKE A NEEDED SHOWER: The latest Film Room makes the case that Denzel Boston Is The Offensive Rookie of the Year Frontrunner (VIP). Deshaun Watson on the sluggish offense: "The Opportunity is Right There in Front of Us." Fred Greetham has his post-practice check-in on the OBR YouTube channel. And in Ask the Insiders, RabidDawg asks Pete Smith why not try a different approach at quarterback. Pete: "makes sense in theory and it's something I've considered, but Gabriel has to prove it can work. That didn't happen in training camp."

And finally. Marvin Harrison Jr. plays his first game for Houston Sunday in London, against Jacksonville. That's Travis Hunter's team. Same agency as Shedeur.

Somebody get me a corkboard and some red string.

Positive news from the world of sports and beyond...

The X-Files Is Officially Returning as Hulu Picks Up Ryan Coogler's Reimagining - "The truth is once again out there," as Space.com puts it. Hulu has ordered a full season of a new X-Files from Ryan Coogler ("Creed," "Black Panther," "Sinners"), who wrote and directed the pilot. Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel star as "two highly decorated but vastly different FBI agents" stuck in a long-shuttered division for unexplained phenomena, Chris Carter is an executive producer, and Steve Buscemi is in the cast, which feels right. So Hulu now has a scripted show about the Cleveland Browns and another about things nobody can explain. Some would call that redundant.

When not representing himself (poorly) since the mid 1990s., Barry McBride is the Publisher and Founder of the OBR and bloviates this nonsense every morning. You can follow him on Twitter @barrymcbride or write him at barry@theobr.com if you are so compelled.

CONTACT Barry to sponsor the OBR. We have plans for nearly any budget!

If you have made it this far, you must subscribe to the OBR. Them's the rules.

articles.title: Tennessee Titans vs. Indianapolis Colts: 5 storylines to watch in Week 6
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans travel to Indianapolis this Sunday as pressure mounts on the offense to finally improve.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans will try to get back on track on Sunday as they travel to Indianapolis to take on the Colts in Week 6.

The Titans completely imploded against the Houston Texans in Week 5 and clearly took a step back against their division rivals. Cam Ward and the offense were bad, but the futility was a team effort that reaches from the press box to offensive coordinator Brian Daboll. Tennessee's defense was better than the offense, but that isn't much to ask.

This will not be easy, and the Titans enter the week as heavy underdogs again. But to move forward and finally break into the win column, they need to start executing, and one of their leaders needs to step up and make a game-changing play.

Here are the top five storylines in the Titans-Colts Week 6 matchup.

Is Dan Moore the worst left tackle in the NFL?

Calling Moore's outing against the Texans rough would be an understatement. Texans' edge, Danielle Hunter, completely manhandled Moore. Between his inability to hold up in pass protection and penalties, Moore completely decimated Tennessee's game plan.

The Titans gave Moore an $82 million mega contract in 2025 as a free agent, and he hasn't shown anything but a few viral videos of his on-field abilities to justify it. With a potential out this offseason, Moore may be playing himself out of Nashville with every snap.

Is the problem Cam Ward, or is it Brian Daboll?

This is a huge debate on social media, and many different perspectives are floating around. You can argue either way, but Ward isn't the only reason the offense is struggling. Even head coach Robert Saleh has addressed some major issues and highlighted one that weighs heavily on fans: the lack of identity, and it falls completely on Daboll.

The Titans' offense has struggled all season, and Ward appears to have regressed in his second season, looking nothing like the quarterback that finished 2025 under Bo Hardegree.

With no signs that Tennessee will move on from Ward soon, the Ward vs. Daboll debate may be far from over.

With all the struggles Tennessee has had in 2026, some fans and media outlets have speculated that Tennessee should go into full rebuild mode and trade their star defender.

While a move like this seems unlikely, it is something to monitor in the coming weeks if things don't turn around.

Division matchups are always important, and the Titans have said being competitive and winning in their division is one of the organization's biggest goals. The Titans failed miserably in their first divisional matchup with Houston, are on an extended losing streak in the AFC South, and need to turn things around.

Does Amy Adams Strunk or spokesperson Burke Nihill need to speak?

The Titans have made some business-side front-office changes in the past few weeks, and now some Nashville media outlets are stirring the pot, calling for a statement on the disappointing start to the season.

While there is a lot of disappointment and frustration, a statement or interview from Strunk or Nihill won't fix the deficiencies on the field. When Strunk streamlined the organization before the coaching search, she stated that the general manager, Mike Borgonzi, had full control of football operations and reported directly to her.

Yes, Titans fans (and especially the local media) are frustrated by the silence about the rough start, but there is no need to burn the organization down, and everyone needs to realize that neither Strunk nor Nihill has to cater to their demands.

Ironically, if Strunk or Nihill had a hand in every decision the team made on the field, like some other owners, these same voices stirring the pot would be screaming to keep them focused on business. That's life in the NFL when losing.

articles.title: Four Notre Dame standouts get nod for PFF College's mock ‘27 NFL draft
articles.summary: PFF College recently unveiled its first mock 2027 NFL Draft of the season. Four Notre Dame standouts made the list, including three defenders.
articles.body:
US LBM Coaches Poll No. 2 Notre Dame has plenty of talent this season that's worthy enough to get their name called at the 2027 NFL draft.

PFF College recently unveiled its first mock NFL draft of the season – and four Fighting Irish standouts have made the cut in the first-round projections.

Gordon McGuinness of PFF College noted in his report that the Los Angeles Chargers will pick cornerback Leonard Moore second overall.

Moore has eight tackles and four pass deflections so far this season.

"The Chargers (could) grab arguably the best defensive prospect in the draft in Moore," McGuinness said. "The Notre Dame standout has allowed just six receptions across 130 coverage snaps this season."

Quarterback CJ Carr comes in as a projected ninth overall selection by the New York Jets. Through six games, Carr has completed 70.8% of his passes for 1,378 yards, 16 touchdowns and a 186.7 QB rating.

"With three first-round picks, it's hard for the Jets to pass up the opportunity to select a quarterback with one of them," McGuinness said. "Carr has enjoyed an incredible start to the 2026 season, earning a 91.2 PFF passing grade and producing a 7.9% big-time throw rate compared to a 2.5% turnover-worthy play rate."

See photos of Notre Dame's 58-7 win over the Stanford Cardinal

Safety Brauntae Johnson tabbed as the No. 27 pick by the Jacksonville Jaguars. Despite not playing since Notre Dame's season opener against Wisconsin due to a foot injury, McGuinness is confident that Johnson is still a first-round selection.

"He was excellent in 2025, though, earning an 82.8 PFF grade and missing just two of his 46 attempted solo tackles," McGuinness added.

Lastly, McGuinness has linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa as the 30th pick by the Minnesota Vikings. Viliamu-Asa has missed a couple of games with injuries, but the junior has 13 tackles and an interception through four games.

"I'm not sure there's a fit I love more in this mock draft than putting Viliamu-Asa in a Brian Flores (Vikings') defense," McGuinness said. "He has missed just 7.7% of his attempted tackles, earned a 91.2 PFF run-defense grade and proven to be an effective blitzer, generating eight pressures on 18 pass-rushing snaps so far this season."

articles.title: ‘It’s Time to File the Divorce Papers,’ ‘Get Him in a West Coast System’ — Ex-Chargers DT Floats ‘Ideal’ Justin Herbert Trade Scenario Away From L.A.
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers’ winless start to the 2026 NFL season has prompted fresh questions about Justin Herbert’s future. Former Chargers defensive tackle B...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers' winless start to the 2026 NFL season has prompted fresh questions about Justin Herbert's future. Former Chargers defensive tackle Breiden Fehoko believes the Minnesota Vikings could offer the quarterback a better situation.

Fehoko has proposed a blockbuster trade that would send Herbert to Minnesota and believes Kevin O'Connell's offensive system and the Vikings' supporting cast could help the quarterback find success away from Los Angeles.

Breiden Fehoko Proposes Justin Herbert Trade to Vikings

Fehoko shared a segment from his podcast, The Fehoko Show, on X, arguing that the Chargers and Herbert should part ways.

"There's only one solution that helps Justin Herbert and the Chargers," Fehoko wrote in the caption. "It lies in Minneapolis, Minnesota. It's time to file the divorce papers and say his final goodbye to Los Angeles. It hasn't worked and WILL NOT WORK."

The proposed move comes after a difficult opening to the season for Herbert and the Chargers. Los Angeles has started 0-5, while Minnesota has won its first five games. The teams have experienced different results despite having clear needs on offense.

Herbert has thrown for 937 yards, five touchdowns, and seven interceptions through five games. Meanwhile, the Chargers have averaged just 16.8 points per game, ranking second-to-last in PFN NFL Offense Score %20assigns,red%20zone%20and%20third%20downs.) list with a 68.6 grade through five weeks, leaving head coach Jim Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel under pressure to find answers.

Fehoko believes a change of system could help Herbert regain his form. He pointed to O'Connell's offense as a potential fit for the quarterback.

"Get him with a Kevin O'Connell," Fehoko said. "Let's get him in a West Coast system, under-center play-action pass, deep shots, short throws, run game. Imagine that."

The Vikings also have Justin Jefferson, one of the NFL's top wide receivers, and a defense coordinated by Brian Flores. That combination could give Herbert a stronger supporting cast if Minnesota pursued the deal.

However, Fehoko acknowledged that acquiring the Chargers quarterback would require a significant offer.

"Okay, obviously, the Vikings receive Justin Herbert now. What's the asking price, and what are you gonna have to pay for Justin Herbert? Pretty steep," he said.

"The Chargers will receive a 2027 first-round pick, the Vikings' 2028 first-round pick, the Vikings' 2029 first-round pick, the Vikings' 2027 third-round pick, and Dallas Turner, edge rusher," Fehoko mentioned.

The proposed deal would give the Chargers valuable draft capital and another young edge rusher. Fehoko argued that Turner could help address their defensive needs as Khalil Mack approaches retirement and contract talks with Tuli Tuipulotu remain unresolved.

He also noted that Los Angeles drafted Akheem Mesidor, giving the team another young defensive player to develop alongside Turner.

"You get Dallas Turner, an edge rusher who — he's not going to be market price. He ain't gonna be 30 million dollars a year, 35 million, 40 million. Ain't gonna be that," Fehoko said, referring to Turner's potential contract cost compared with established edge rushers.

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

For Minnesota, Herbert could strengthen an offense that needs more consistent production. Pairing him with Jefferson under O'Connell could give the Vikings a more dangerous passing attack.

Still, the proposal remains hypothetical. The Chargers have treated Herbert as their franchise quarterback, and a trade would require major changes to their plans.

Fehoko nevertheless called Minnesota the "ideal trade" partner for Herbert, even if the quarterback's no-trade clause complicates negotiations. So, right now, the Chargers must focus on ending their losing streak while trade speculation continues to swirl around their struggling season.

articles.title: Breaking Down Thursday Night Football Between Denver And Seattle
articles.summary: Thursday Night Football Odds Denver Broncos Seattle Seahawks prediction pick and what do the oddsmakers say about laying the points and over under betting.
articles.body:
Tonight's NFL offering is a good one. This isn't necessarily a Super Bowl preview but it is the most attractive matchup of the week. Both teams are dinged up at key positions and Denver has a bit of an offensive identity issue.

Sean Payton has taken over play calling so it will be interesting to see how much (or little) changes for the Broncos. One thing's for sure, he needs to figure out how to slow down Seattle's pass rush.

Last week our NFL picks were hot . These odds are from Caesars.

Seattle at Denver (+2.5) Over/under 40.5 Thursday 8 p.m. Amazon Prime

Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Broncos CB1 Patrick Surtain II are both dealing with bum ankles. The biggest one-on-one matchup may not be as front and center as we hope it will be. Still, both will play. It's more important for Surtain to be 100%. If he's not, a healthy(ish) JSN will cook him. That is, if Sam Darnold stops throwing interceptions. He's falling into old habits already this year. I still give the edge slightly to Seattle's offense.

Denver can't run the ball. Averaging about 86 yards a game won't get it done when you have to neutralize a pretty fierce pass rush. The last three weeks however havent been the Seahawks' best on defense. They've given up about 28.5 a game over that stretch (two losses). Sean Payton needs to figure out how to keep Bo Nix upright and efficient. Once again edge to Seattle.

It's going to come down to who the steadier quarterback is. Darnold has thrown five interceptions and been sacked eight times in the last three games. Nix has one turnover but his completion percentage over three games is only 56.3%. That simply will not do in this league anymore, especially against a defense the caliber of Seattle.

What do the oddsmakers say? Home underdogs getting 3.5 points or less are covering at about a 52% clip so far this year. So this is a toss up in that regard. Both teams are 5-0 in their last five Thursday games combined. Something has to give.

Bottom line: Denver can't run the ball. Their secondary is banged up. Their offense won't fix itself in a week. A saving grace may be Seattle's propensity to give up 28 a game lately. Being at home will give the Broncos a small boost. It probably won't be enough.

The play: Lay the points. It may be a close one but Seattle absolutely can't afford to fall another game back in the NFC West. They may not be able to catch San Francisco anyway but the Rams are looming. I mean, as long as they can find a kicker. This is not a must win yet for Seattle, but close.

Take the over on the total also, 40.5 seems a touch low despite the good defenses involved. This one will have a few more points scored than you might think.

articles.title: Terry Bradshaw struggled with anxiety attacks and extreme emotions; now, he’s sharing his story of surviving depression
articles.summary: Terry Bradshaw spent years dealing with anxiety attacks and sharp emotional swings without fully understanding what was happening.
articles.body: Terry Bradshaw spent years dealing with anxiety attacks and sharp emotional swings without fully understanding what was happening. The former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback, now 78, was diagnosed with clinical depression in the late 1990s, after retiring from football. He is speaking openly about that experience in his new memoir, Looking for Terry, released on October 13. Bradshaw wants readers to understand that depression is an illness, not a personal failing. His account also sheds light on why asking for help was so difficult, especially for a high-profile male athlete.Terry Bradshaw opens up about years of anxiety and depressionBradshaw says his emotional struggles began long before he received a diagnosis. Growing up in Shreveport, Louisiana, he believes he had undiagnosed ADHD. Anxiety attacks followed, and the pressure of playing quarterback for the Steelers brought emotional highs and lows that he initially accepted as normal.“You didn’t talk about it,” he tells PEOPLE.That silence became harder to maintain as his career grew. Bradshaw was one of the NFL's biggest names, and admitting that he needed help meant confronting the idea that showing vulnerability could make him look weak.“Finally saying, ‘Hey, I’m really f----d up. I need to get some help,’ ” was one of the “hardest things” Terry ever did.He eventually sought support from a therapist, a psychiatrist and a pastor. His formal depression diagnosis came in the late 1990s, after his playing career had ended and his broadcasting work was gaining momentum.Bradshaw's experience challenges the assumption that success makes personal struggles easier to manage. He had won four Super Bowls and built a second career on television, yet neither achievement kept depression away.“It is an ugly disease,” he tells PEOPLE, stressing the importance of having a “good support group.”His memoir, Looking for Terry, also covers his football career, life beyond the NFL and recent back-to-back cancer diagnoses. Bradshaw hopes sharing these experiences will help readers recognise that personal struggles can exist alongside professional success.How Tammy Bradshaw helped him change his outlookBradshaw credits his wife, Tammy, with helping him understand his condition and speak about it without shame. The couple met in the early 2000s and married in 2014. Tammy, a former radiation therapist, helped him see depression as something he did not choose and should not blame himself for.“This is not a choice. This isn’t the consequence of something you’ve done. It’s not your fault.”That understanding has changed how the couple handles difficult days. Bradshaw says he can now tell his wife when he is struggling, rather than trying to conceal what he feels.“She just gets me out of it. She gets my mind off of it. She frees me up. We do something. We talk about it.”Tammy can often recognise when he is having a hard time just by looking at him. The couple even has a name for those moments: “Roy.” When Bradshaw feels low, they acknowledge that “Roy” has come to visit.“I may be emotional about it, but I’m totally comfortable with telling her,” he says. “Men think that’s a weakness. I got past it being a weakness. It’s a sickness.”For Bradshaw, that distinction is central to the message he wants readers to take from his story. “There’s nothing wrong with admitting you’ve got issues,” he says.Life on the couple's 155-acre Texas ranch, purchased in 2023, has also brought him peace through horse breeding. Yet Bradshaw is not presenting his story as a struggle he has permanently left behind. Instead, he wants people dealing with depression to speak with loved ones and seek professional help.“Tammy says I’m an open book,” he says. “I like being an open book.”His reflection on the journey is simple: “I’m proud of myself for making it through and surviving.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
Longtime Philadelphia Eagles offensive guard Landon Dickerson implied his future with the team is out of his hands after the team has seen a major shakeup to the line.

Asked Wednesday whether he considers himself the "long-term left guard" in Philly, the three-time Pro Bowler responded with another question: "Is that really my decision?"

Fourteen-year veteran Lane Johnson retired and the Eagles traded interior lineman Cam Jurgens to the Baltimore Ravens. The team isn't in a rebuild per se following a 2-3 start, but the short-term priorities might be a little different now than they were to begin the year.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Philadelphia isn't expected to have a major sell-off, but that won't stop rival teams from inquiring about certain veterans.

Dickerson is one such example, with Rapoport writing that "it would not surprise those in the league if teams start calling" on him.

The 28-year-old is in the first year of his $58 million extension, which runs through 2028. His $19.5 million average salary is eighth at his position.

If they were to trade him, the Eagles would probably be doing so for financial purposes rather than as a reflection of their belief that Dickerson's performance will start to decline.

Philly has yet to fully activate Dickerson from injured reserve, opening his practice window Wednesday. That's putting the brakes on any hypothetical trade for the time being.

It may not be right up until the Nov. 10 deadline that there's firm clarity over his status with the Eagles for the remainder of the campaign.

articles.summary: Earlier this year, Travis Kelce earned recognition for his work off the field when the Kansas City Chiefs named him their club winner for the 2025 Walter
articles.body: Earlier this year, Travis Kelce earned recognition for his work off the field when the Kansas City Chiefs named him their club winner for the 2025 Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year Award. But the tight end’s charitable efforts soon faced difficult questions. An investigation by The Arizona Republic examined the finances of his Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation, raising concerns about how much money reached charitable programmes and how the organisation handled its expenses. The findings have put the foundation’s financial reporting and governance under scrutiny, even as Kelce weighs important decisions about his NFL future.Travis Kelce’s charity foundation faces questions over spendingFederal tax records reviewed by The Arizona Republic showed that Eighty-Seven and Running reported spending just 41 cents of every dollar on charitable activities between 2021 and 2024. The investigation also found that the foundation paid hundreds of thousands of dollars to A&A Management Group, a company co-founded by Kelce’s longtime business managers, Aaron and Andre Eanes.The report raised further concerns about the foundation’s structure. According to the investigation, the organisation had no officially listed president, secretary or treasurer and operated with only two board members. That fell short of the three-member minimum cited in the report as necessary for proper oversight.Laurie Styron, executive director of CharityWatch, reviewed the foundation’s tax filings for The Arizona Republic and questioned the relationship between the nonprofit and the management company.“It appears to function more as an extension of the management company versus as an independent public charity,” Styron said. “That’s not how charities work. It’s wrong.”The figures also suggested that only 56 cents of every dollar spent had gone towards charity since the foundation began operating. Those findings have drawn attention to the distinction between the money a nonprofit raises, its operating expenses and the funds it directs towards its charitable mission.However, the reported figures do not, on their own, establish that funds were misused. The foundation’s representatives have disputed the suggestion that the records accurately reflect its charitable work.Travis Kelce’s representatives respond to the financial concernsAaron Eanes attributed the reported spending figures to errors in the foundation’s tax filings. He said expenses connected to charitable programmes had been incorrectly classified as management costs rather than properly allocated to programme services.Eanes told The Arizona Republic that the records therefore did not provide an accurate “indication of where the resources were truly directed,” he claimed.He also pointed to changes in the foundation’s financial reporting, saying, “We have since corrected this: Management fees decreased significantly in 2024 and dropped to zero in 2025.”Eanes added that the organisation planned to strengthen its oversight and improve transparency.“Looking ahead, we are expanding our board of directors, bringing on advisers with nonprofit expertise, and restructuring our reporting processes to better reflect our actual program work. We are dedicated to ensuring this foundation operates at the highest standards,” he added.The planned changes could help address concerns about accountability, but the foundation’s financial reporting remains central to the debate. The Cowboys are allowing the second-most yards per game (395.4) after finishing 30th in the category in 2025.

Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown said he and his defensive peers chatted behind closed doors following a 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The purpose of the meeting was "looking ourselves in the mirror."

"Putting what we wanted our standard to be, we put that on the board. We went by bullet point, bullet point," he said, per Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site. "Are we holding up to this? Are we being this? As a unit, how can we get closer? What is it? Just hearing from all of us. It really wasn't like a fire drill conversation, it was more so, 'What can I do to help you? What do I expect from you on Sundays, or every Monday walk throughs?'"

Head coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Wednesday he was encouraged by his players taking the initiative and holding themselves accountable:

Of course, a coach in Schottenheimer's position isn't going to say anything else publicly. Taking any other tack would risk alienating his players and/or fellow coaches.

The players-only meeting is coupled with the arrival of Mike Pettine, an experienced NFL coach and coordinator. He has the title of senior defensive assistant to defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who will start working from the booth instead of the sideline.

Add it all together and Tomlin's conclusion might be astute. The Cowboys are in trouble and lacking in solutions to turn around what's one of the NFL's worst defenses.
