articles.body:
New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson understands the importance of his team's crucial AFC East battle with the host New England Patriots on Sunday afternoon.

"There's a premium on this one because it is our first one [in the division]," Wilson told reporters on Wednesday. "I don't know how to exactly put it, but it's a big-ass game."

It sure is. The 2-3 Jets are a game behind the 3-2 Patriots, who sit second in the division below the 4-1 Bills. A loss to New England puts the Jets two full games back (and without the head-to-head tiebreaker). A win, of course, evens the Jets and Pats and gives New York the tiebreaker for now.

There's a deeper meaning to this game, of course. As ESPN's Rich Cimini noted, the Jets have gone 13-47 in the AFC East since 2010. Wilson has experienced some of that divisional struggle, with the Jets going 6-18 since he got drafted in 2022.

In addition, New York hasn't made the playoffs since 2010, losing 10 or more games in 11 of those seasons. In most years, the Jets' playoff hopes evaporate well before the regular season, but 2026 has the chance to tell a much better tale.

New York has played hard and competed in head coach Aaron Glenn's second season. The defense in particular has been exceptional, with the Jets allowing the fifth-fewest points per game.

They're heading into the New Englnd off the strength of a hard-fought, gritty 17-12 home win over the Cleveland Browns, so the Jets arrive into town with some momentum. The Pats do as well, though, as winners of two straight.

We'll see how things go soon enough. Kickoff at Gilette Stadium is set for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

articles.title: “I felt it was extremely important to give back”: How Justin Herbert’s $25,000 donation helped provide 100,000 meals to families in Los Angeles
articles.summary: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has given fans plenty to cheer about on the football field. But in Dec.
articles.body: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has given fans plenty to cheer about on the football field. But in Dec. 2021, he made headlines for something beyond football. Herbert donated $25,000 to the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank, helping provide 100,000 meals to children and families across Los Angeles County. The donation arrived just before the holidays, when many families were struggling to put food on the table.The gesture was also very personal for the QB He credited his parents for teaching him to help others and said he wanted to support the community he called home. At a time when many people were still dealing with the effects of the pandemic, the Chargers quarterback wanted to do his part. Justin Herbert's $25,000 donation helped put 100,000 meals on the tableOn Dec. 15, 2021, the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank announced Herbert's $25,000 contribution. The donation was enough to help distribute 100,000 meals throughout Los Angeles County during the holiday season.The need remained high even as life began returning to normal for some people. Families across the county continued to face food insecurity, with many still feeling the financial effects of the COVID-19 pandemic. The Food Bank reported that it was distributing more than twice as much food as it had before the pandemic.Herbert wanted to help his neighbours through that difficult period. In a statement released by the organisation, he explained what had inspired him to make the donation."My parents always instilled in my brothers and me the importance of service to others," Herbert said. "As a member of this community, I felt it was extremely important to give back and support my neighbors. People are in need, and it's our job to come together and help."His words reflected the values his family had taught him. Rather than treating charitable work as something separate from his life as an NFL player, Herbert saw it as a responsibility to the people around him.The contribution also built on the Los Angeles Chargers' earlier support for the same organisation. During the pandemic, the team had made a significant donation to help people affected by layoffs and reduced working hours. Why the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank needed support during the holidaysThe Los Angeles Regional Food Bank had been working to fight hunger in the county since 1973. Its network of 700 partner agencies helped distribute food and groceries to people who needed assistance, including children and families facing financial hardship.At the time of Herbert's donation, the organisation was providing food assistance to an average of 900,000 people every month. It also relied on donations and the efforts of around 15,000 volunteers to keep its programmes running.The Food Bank's donation model helped make contributions go further. According to the organisation, every dollar donated could provide four meals to someone facing food insecurity. Herbert's $25,000 gift therefore offered meaningful support during a particularly difficult time of year.Michael Flood, the organisation's president and CEO, expressed his gratitude for the quarterback's contribution. He noted that although the numbers had fallen from their pandemic peak, the Food Bank was still distributing more than twice the amount of food it had handled before the outbreak.Flood's comments highlighted the ongoing challenge facing families across Los Angeles County. The holiday season can bring additional pressure for households already struggling with everyday expenses, making community support especially valuable.Herbert's donation helped the organisation continue its work when many families needed assistance. It also showed how an individual contribution, backed by a local charity's distribution network, could reach people across a large community.In Justin’s case, the gesture came down to a simple belief: people should help one another when they can. articles.title: Troy Aikman responds to reported MNF contract tensions with Joe Buck: 'I'm looking forward to … where my next landing spot might be'
articles.summary: Joe Buck has signed a $100 million extension with ESPN, but Troy Aikman still has not.
articles.body:
Tensions are apparently running high inside the "Monday Night Football" booth.

Longtime broadcaster Joe Buck and Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman got into an argument inside the announcer booth at SoFi Stadium ahead of Monday night's game between the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills, according to Front Office Sports' Ryan Glasspiegel .

Buck and Aikman's relationship has reportedly been strained ever since Buck reportedly reached a new contract with ESPN last month that is reportedly worth more than $100 million over the next six seasons. The new deal will ensure that Buck will call the Super Bowl both this year and again when ESPN/ABC gets the rights to it in 2031.

Aikman, however, has not received a formal offer on a new deal.

So on Monday night, according to Glasspiegel, Buck "broke the ice" on the unspoken tension between the two. That led to an argument, which eventually de-escalated before the game started. The game carried on normally, and Buck and Aikman called the game without issue.

Asked about tension with his broadcast partner, Aikman told 96.7 The Ticket on Thursday: "There's probably a time and a place for all that to be discussed. I don't know if now is the time. I don't know that it's hard to figure out kind of what's happened. I'll broadcast through this season and I'll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens. I'm looking forward to whatever the rest of this year does hold with the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot might be."

Aikman spent 12 seasons playing with the Cowboys, and he led the franchise to three Super Bowl titles before he retired after the 2000 campaign. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2006.

Aikman quickly transitioned into broadcasting after his playing career ended, and he joined Buck at Fox in 2002. The pair are the longest-tenured broadcast team in NFL history, and have undoubtedly become among the most recognizable voices in the sport. They left Fox for ESPN in 2022. Aikman reached his contract with ESPN first, and Buck followed weeks later.

It's not known what would happen to Aikman should he split with ESPN after the Super Bowl. While there are several potential landing spots for him at other networks, an NFL world without the Aikman-Buck pairing is one that the sport hasn't seen in decades.

articles.title: Week 6 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys and Packers had much different results last week
articles.summary: The Packers rebounded in a big way last week, while the Cowboys fell apart. Here are my ATS picks for every Week 6 game.
articles.body:
One week can change the entire perception of an NFL team — sometimes that's good, sometimes it's not.

The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers were both 2-2 coming into last week's games. The Cowboys weren't considered a Super Bowl contender, but they were at least looking OK — especially in a bad NFC East — with a home game against the winless Buccaneers coming up. The Packers had played so poorly through four weeks that they were home underdogs to the Bears for the first time in 20 years , even though Chicago was starting its backup quarterback.

The Cowboys and Packers come into Week 6's Sunday night game with their seasons flipped around.

The Cowboys looked horrible against the Buccaneers, losing to an undrafted rookie quarterback in Jalon Daniels. The defensive problems finally got to a point in which the Cowboys hired longtime NFL defensive coordinator Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant and said defensive coordinator Christian Parker will now call plays from the press box. There's always some angst in Dallas because of the attention on the Cowboys all the time, but it's not like the defensive problems are made up. Dallas was last in defensive DVOA last season and they're last so far this season.

Meanwhile, the talk of Matt LaFleur being on the hot seat seems like it was a lot longer than a week ago. The best way to gain back the confidence of Packers fans is to blow out the Bears, and the Packers did just that. They blasted Chicago, 31-7, with Jordan Love embarrassing the Bears defense with his deep passing and Green Bay shutting down everything Chicago's offense wanted to do. After not playing a good game through four weeks, the Packers played a great game in Week 5.

That makes Week 6 hard to figure out. Do the Cowboys rebound or is the defense simply unfixable? What's the real Packers team — the one that couldn't run the ball, couldn't protect Love and had a below-average defense through four games, or the one we saw Sunday?

The Packers are small favorites Sunday night, indicating the oddsmakers don't have a lot of confidence in them still. But it's tougher to bank on the Cowboys' defense. Packers -1.5 is the pick , though it could all look different for both teams next week. That's how the NFL goes.

Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 6 of the NFL season:

Not all is great for the defending champs, who can't run the ball and still don't have an offensive option other than Jaxon Smith-Njigba. But they've been far better than the Broncos, who were on their way to losing to the winless and injury-plagued Chargers before saving themselves with a fourth-quarter rally. The matchup of Seattle's defense against an aimless Broncos offense is enough to take the Seahawks.

A bit of a weird line. The Jaguars are 4-1 and while last week's miracle win over the Eagles wasn't great, they do look like a legitimate contender in the AFC. The Texans are 1-4 and their lone win came against the 0-5 Titans. And yet, in a neutral site game — if either team has the edge it's Jacksonville, who does the London trip every season and stayed overseas after playing there last week — the Jaguars aren't even giving a full field goal. Yes it's a desperate Houston team with a very good defense, but it's not a lot of respect for the Jaguars.

It appears Michael Penix Jr. and Caleb Williams will start, which should make for an entertaining game. The big question for this one will be what to make of the Bears defense. In Week 1 and 5 they gave up 68 combined points. From Weeks 2-4 they allowed 28 points. The hot stretch in the middle could have come from facing three bad offenses (Vikings without Kyler Murray in bad weather, Eagles, Jets) instead of the Panthers and Packers, their other two opponents who both scored more than 30 points. The Falcons are a good offense with Penix, so points should be coming.

The Ravens should have confidence after beating the Falcons without Lamar Jackson last week. However, a Tyler Huntley offense still isn't one I'm comfortable laying 5.5 points with on the road.

Metrics like DVOA and net EPA per play say these teams are practically even. The Buccaneers have the rest advantage, having played last Thursday night, and the Steelers are 0-2 on the road (3-0 at home). Daniels could be exposed by the best defense he's faced, but it's also not the intimidating Steelers defense from recent years.

The Patriots are officially warmed up. The start to the season was lackluster, but Drake Maye is coming off two good games in a row. The Jets are better than some expected, but they're facing a team that has its season back on track and wants to keep that going.

It's hard to buy the Giants. There's no evidence they're a good team despite their 3-1-1 record. But it's not like there are any signs that the Saints are much better. New Orleans is 30th in DVOA ahead of only the hopeless Titans and Dolphins. Anything can happen when Jameis Winston is starting at quarterback, good or bad — good luck predicting it.

It's weird to see the Panthers favored at Philadelphia (though some books have the Eagles as a small favorite). But to this point, Carolina has been the far better team. Also, they're coming off a bye while the Eagles come right off a flight from London, where they took a horrific loss after kicking a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left.

The Titans should be very happy the Dolphins exist, or else there would be even more talk about how bad they are. Indianapolis hasn't been great, either, but it's just too difficult to take the Titans right now.

It's quite possible the Rams take out their frustrations on the Cardinals. Los Angeles is 2-3, but the schedule has been tough and it starts to ease up with a game against Arizona, which just got throttled by the Lions. The Cardinals seem to be running out of steam after looking decent to start the season. Still, 12.5 points is a lot considering the Rams haven't looked great yet, and Arizona can move the ball, especially in garbage time.

The Bills are coming off an emotional, difficult overtime win against the Rams on Monday night. They are the better team, but that's a tough situational spot, and the Raiders are not as bad as they looked last week against the Patriots. Let's give Vegas one more shot to show that 3-0 start wasn't fraudulent.

The Chargers aren't just bad, they're injured. They held their own against the Broncos last week, but that probably says more about Denver. This season is already ugly for Los Angeles and it's not going to get much better.

If the Commanders aren't completely downtrodden after one of the dumbest endings in recent NFL history last week, in which they casually watched the final minute of overtime run out without getting a field-goal attempt, then this seems like too many points. The 49ers have played very well on both sides of the ball (the defense has been a great surprise), but there is some danger of a letdown after winning at Seattle. Take the points and hope last week's fiasco doesn't still linger for Washington.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy's Usage Explained by Giants' John Harbaugh, Teases Expanded Role for QB
articles.summary: After making his New York Giants' debut in Sunday's tie with the Washington Commanders, J.J. McCarthy could start to get more playing time going forward as head coach John Harbaugh evaluates ways to boost the offense.
articles.body:
After making his New York Giants' debut in Sunday's tie with the Washington Commanders, J.J. McCarthy could start to get more playing time going forward as head coach John Harbaugh evaluates ways to boost the offense.

Harbaugh told reporters during his weekly press conference that using McCarthy as a "change of pace" against the Commanders could lead to more opportunities for him in ways that don't necessarily require him to play every snap:

"The benefits of it? It's a change of pace. What you saw is probably not all we have for him right now. Whether or not he's out there or not will be determined based on whatever happens. But we'll see if it's something that can help us. One thing about it, to me, it's like, what's the benefit of not doing everything you can to use all the guys you have? We're always going to be searching for opportunities to use our players, give them an opportunity to help us win games. I think we'd be negligent if we didn't try to do that."

The Giants acquired McCarthy, the No. 10 pick in the 2024 NFL draft, from the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 28. New York only had to give up a fifth-round selection in the 2027 draft in the deal.

McCarthy played five snaps against the Commanders. He ran for two yards on two carries and two other plays were negated by penalties. It was his first regular-season appearance since Week 18 with the Vikings in 2025.

After Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 2, the Giants were in a tough spot at quarterback. Jameis Winston is a capable backup, but his volatility also makes him hard to rely on week after week.

McCarthy's lone season as a starter with the Vikings in 2025 didn't inspire much confidence in his long-term outlook, but he is only 23 with just 10 games of NFL experience under his belt coming into this year.

The Giants lead the NFC East with a 3-1-1 record, though two of those wins are over arguably the two worst teams in the NFL — Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals.

Their next two games going into the bye are against the New Orleans Saints and Houston Texans. Those matchups could determine their path forward and how much playing time McCarthy might see when they come out of their bye in Week 8.

articles.title: Troy Aikman Discusses ESPN Contract Situation, 'Monday Night Football' Status Amid Rumors on Future
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys legend Troy Aikman may have tipped his hand as to his future on the Monday Night Football broadcast.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys legend Troy Aikman may have tipped his hand as to his future on the Monday Night Football broadcast.

During an appearance on 96.7 The Ticket in Dallas (via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News ), Aikman addressed a report from Front Office Sports' Ryan Glasspiegel about "tension" between him and longtime broadcast partner Joe Buck.

"There's probably a time and a place for all that. I don't know if now is the time," Aikman said. "I don't know if it's hard to figure out kind of what happened. I'll broadcast through this season and I'll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens. I'm looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot may be."

Tyreek Hill's Agent Still Talking to Teams

Whether intentional or not, the retired quarterback seemingly revealed a lot while trying to avoid addressing his long-term status directly. He doesn't sound like somebody who's imminently planning to sign a new contract after Buck already did .

Aikman began his broadcasting career with Fox in 2001, the year after his playing career ended. He started working alongside Buck in 2002, and they jumped ship together for ESPN and Monday Night Football in 2022.

According to Glasspiegel, Aikman's contract is at the heart of the discord: "There has been unspoken tension between the partners that one has a new contract while the other, Aikman, has not received a formal offer."

Beyond the financial component, this could be a byproduct of Aikman and Buck working together for so long. Maybe they're ready for a change after more than 20 years.

ESPN spent big in order to bring some stability to its MNF broadcast after years of turnover. Now, it might be back in search of a lead color commentator.

articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Broncos and Seahawks trying to rediscover last season's success
articles.summary: The Broncos and Seahawks are 3-2 but there are concerns for both teams.
articles.body:
Had it not been for a surprising quarterback injury, one terrible turnover in the AFC championship game and a blizzard after that, Thursday night might be a Super Bowl rematch.

The Denver Broncos were 14-3 last season but had to play the AFC title game in the snow without quarterback Bo Nix, who broke his ankle at the end of a divisional-round playoff win over the Buffalo Bills. They lost to the New England Patriots, with backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham having a bad fumble deep in his own territory that flipped the game, and not much has gone right since.

The Seattle Seahawks won the Super Bowl, but, like the Broncos, the start to this season has been tougher.

Those teams combined to go 32-7 last season. This season they're a combined 6-4 and given Denver's struggles, it's fortunate that record is above .500. And one of these two teams, barring a tie, will dip to 3-3 after they face off Thursday night.

Seattle's issues aren't as bad. Its defense is still elite. But the Seahawks' offense has flaws . The running game has been poor with Kenneth Walker III leaving in free agency to Kansas City, and the passing game is getting almost nothing from anyone other than Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Sam Darnold is turning it over at a troubling rate, with five interceptions over his last three games since returning from injury. Still, it seems likely the Seahawks will get it together.

The Broncos are really struggling. They've managed a 3-2 record and they had a tough schedule to start the season, so maybe there are better days ahead. But they had a hard time against an injury-ravaged Chargers team last week, needing a fourth-quarter rally to win. The offense switched play-callers from coordinator Davis Webb to head coach Sean Payton after four weeks, and the results last week weren't much different. Bo Nix had just 123 passing yards against the Chargers, and his passer rating is a career worst 80.8. Denver is 26th in points scored and 30th in yards gained. The Broncos had promising second-half rallies to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars and Los Angeles Rams, and those are two high quality wins, but the other eight halves this season haven't been pretty.

Last season was a surprising success for the Seahawks and Broncos. The beginning of this season hasn't been as kind, but a win Thursday night would help.

For Seattle, falling three losses behind the 49ers in the NFC West this early in the season would not be great. But nobody would be too worried about the Seahawks, even if they're 3-3. There are some concerns over how they've looked this season but they have a solid foundation.

A loss by the Broncos should bring about some worry. They'd also fall three losses behind the undefeated first-place team in their division (Kansas City), and Denver has yet to have one good 60-minute performance this season. A win over Seattle would ease plenty of worries about their long-term viability, but a loss would hurt.

The Broncos should feel urgency to get a win.

The Broncos' secondary is banged up. Star cornerback Pat Surtain II and safety Talanoa Hufanga are out . Surtain's absence in particular puts Moss on the spot, assuming he's able to play through a rib injury that limited him in practice. If Moss plays, he's likely to draw Jaxon Smith-Njigba in coverage on many snaps. Smith-Njigba is the reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year and this season leads the NFL with 583 receiving yards. JSN has been limited in practice as well, with an ankle injury. If Smith-Njigba plays, whoever draws him in coverage on the Broncos' side has the most important assignment of the night.

The Broncos (+2.5) are a rare home underdog against the defending champion Seahawks on Thursday night. Seattle lost a heavyweight battle against San Francisco on Sunday, while Denver was far from impressive in a win over the Chargers. Bo Nix and Denver's offense isn't playing well enough to beat Seattle, and without Patrick Surtain, I'm not sure how the Broncos slow down JSN. The public likes Seattle to cover, and I agree.

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Fantasy football storylines, by Scott Pianowski

Points could be hard to come by Thursday, with the Seahawks and Broncos both sitting top 10 in defense, per DVOA (as a result, the total is a modest 40.5). Here are three fantasy themes to track as you watch the game.

1. Can Sean Payton get Bo Nix going? Payton took over the play sheet last week but Denver's offense stayed grounded. Nix charted as the QB5 in the win over the Rams three weeks ago, otherwise he's been a mess all year. Nix is dragging down his teammates; WR Jaylen Waddle has been one of the biggest busts of the season so far.

2. What's the second pitch in the Seattle passing game? Jaxon Smith-Njigba is still an elite wideout, but the Seahawks have struggled to find a second consistent option when they pass. Nobody else on the team is averaging even 30 receiving yards per week, and only JSN has multiple touchdown catches.

3. Can volume save running backs Emanuel Wilson and J.K. Dobbins? Wilson is averaging a marginal 3.4 yards per carry, while Dobbins sits at 3.6. Alas, Wilson has made it to 21 or more touches three times, and Dobbins saw 20 chances last week. Opportunity often trumps talent level as we hunt for running back fantasy value.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer has no issue with Cowboys' players-only meeting after Mike Tomlin criticism
articles.summary: The Cowboys' defense hasn't improved much after a miserable 2025.
articles.body:
After having literally the worst-ranked defense in the NFL last season, the Dallas Cowboys entered 2026 hoping to see significant improvement on that front. But things haven't gone well through five games, resulting in a players-only meeting after the team's surprising loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5.

While it's not necessarily uncommon for players to hold meetings amid a tough stretch, this particular meeting gained extra attention after former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin commented on it.

During an appearance on the "New Heights" podcast with the Kelce brothers, Tomlin said a players-only meeting is rarely a good thing for a coaching staff . "I think you're dead," Tomlin responded when asked how a coach should feel about the situation.

Whether he intended it or not, Tomlin's comment thrust Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer into the spotlight. Schottenheimer was asked about the meeting and Tomlin's comment Wednesday and said he has no issue with the players taking ownership of their struggles, per ESPN.

"I love it," Schottenheimer told reporters Wednesday. "I've said from the very beginning, the best teams I've ever been around are led by the locker room. And my information that I received from some of those guys that called that meeting, it was very productive. It was very open and honest."

Schottenheimer added he wasn't bothered by the meeting and he believes the team's defense will get things turned around.

Cowboys continue to struggle on defense in 2026

After allowing a league-worst 30.1 points per game last season, the Cowboys fired defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus. In an attempt to try to turn things around, Dallas hired Christian Parker from the Philadelphia Eagles.

Through his first five games in that role, Parker hasn't found much success. The Cowboys are allowing 27.2 points per game thus far, which ranks 25th in the NFL. It's an improvement, but only because the team couldn't get any worse.

While no aspect of the team's defense has thrived, the team has particularly struggled against opposing running backs. The Cowboys have already allowed 842 rushing yards on the season, the worst figure in the NFL. Through five games, opposing teams have scored on 48 percent of their offensive drives against the Cowboys, one of the worst rates in the game.

Failure to improve could lead to big changes down the road. Schottenheimer failed to post a winning season in his first year on the job. If the Cowboys struggle again in 2026, both Schottenheimer and Parker could find themselves looking for work.

Fantasy managers may be scrambling to fill starting lineups in Week 6, as both injuries and bye weeks will eliminate options.

articles.title: Week 6 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Fantasy Football Stars to Play and Bench
articles.summary: Week 6 will begin with a battle between teams that made the NFL's final four last season. The Denver Broncos will host the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football.
articles.body:
Week 6 will begin with a battle between teams that made the NFL's final four last season. The Denver Broncos will host the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football .

Thursday's matchup figures to be a star-studded affair, but fantasy managers may find many of their biggest stars absent in Week 6. Injuries have heavily impacted the fantasy landscape to this point, and the Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins, and Minnesota Vikings are on bye this week.

Here, you'll find some start/sit recommendations for second-tier stars in Week 6 based on factors like past performances, projected roles, individual matchups, and point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love looked like a low-end streamer for most of the early season. Then, he exploded for 25.3 fantasy points in a Week 5 romp over the rival Chicago Bears.

Love is still projected as a matchup-based play, but he has a tremendous matchup this week against a struggling Dallas Cowboys defense. Dallas has surrendered the sixth-most fantasy points to opposing QBs this season.

The list of other quarterbacks to start in Week 6 includes:

Broncos quarterback Bo Nix has gotten off to a rocky start, too, though he's unlikely to rebound as Love did on Sunday. Denver's offense is in disarray, and Nix hasn't been making up for his struggles by scrambling as much as he's done in the past.

To this point, Nix has reached 16 fantasy points in only one of five games. He's facing a tough situation on a short week against a terrific Seattle defense.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

While the Packers' offense got going against the Bears, their defense remains a work-in-progress. Green Bay has been particularly vulnerable to the run, which is part of the reason why Cowboys starter Javonte Williams is a strong start this week.

The Packers have surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing RBs.

The other piece of the equation is the reality that Dallas' defense isn't good. The Cowboys should lean on the run in order to keep Love and Co. off the field.

Rhamondre Stevenson, New England Patriots

Sit: Omarion Hampton, Los Angeles Chargers

Like the Broncos' offense, the Los Angeles Chargers offense is still trying to find a rhythm. The marriage between Justin Herbert and new OC Mike McDaniel hasn't gone well so far, and the rest of the unit has suffered.

McDaniel has tried to spark the unit by getting other running backs involved, to the detriment of starter Omarion Hampton. The 2025 first-round pick has only reached double-digit fantasy points twice, is coming off a 4.9-point outing, and faces a stout Kansas City Chiefs defense that is coming off the bye.

San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans hasn't quite returned to the must-start territory he was in earlier in his career. However, he's inching close to it, and the loss of Deebo Samuel to a hamstring strain will only further cement his status as San Francisco's No. 1 receiver.

Evans delivered 26.3 fantasy points last week and has reached double digits in four of five games. This week, he'll face a Washington Commanders defense that has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing WRs.

New England Patriots receiver Romeo Doubs has been very hit-or-miss in his first season with the club. He's reached double-digit fantasy points twice and had 23.8 points in Week 4. However, he had no production at all in the season-opener and is coming off of a 2.6-point outing.

Doubs is unlikely to surge this week against an underrated New York Jets defense. New York has surrendered the ninth-fewest fantasy points to opposing WRs, and the fact that A.J. Brown could return for the Patriots this week only further impacts Doubs' value.

Tomlin's Take After Cowboys' Players-Only Meeting 💀

Los Angeles Rams tight end Tyler Higbee played a huge role in the team's offense on Monday night. While he didn't do enough to give L.A. a win over the Buffalo Bills, he finished with five catches for 83 yards and 13.3 fantasy points.

In Week 3, Higbee topped 20 fantasy points, and he's reached double digits in three straight games. This week, he'll face an Arizona Cardinals defense that has surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points to opposing TEs.

Atlanta Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts hasn't been as involved in Kevin Stefanski's offense as most might have expected. He delivered 15.2 fantasy points in Week 5, but that marked his first double-digit performance of 2026.

This week, the Falcons will host the Chicago Bears, who have surrendered the third-fewest fantasy points to opposing tight ends. Pitts is a matchup-based play with a bad matchup who should be avoided in Week 6.

articles.title: 40% gone: Bengaluru electorate to shrink from 1 crore to 59 lakh
articles.summary: Bengaluru voter rolls may drop from 1 crore to 59 lakh after Karnataka’s special intensive revision; draft roll has 56.9 lakh, plus 2 lakh expected additions.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Electorate size in Bengaluru is set to shrink from a little over 1 crore to around 59 lakh, with nearly 2.2 lakh people submitting Form 6 applications as the special intensive revision of electoral rolls in Karnataka enters the home stretch.Bengaluru Urban district electoral officer and Greater Bengaluru Authority chief commissioner Maheshwar Rao said Thursday the draft electoral roll contains 56.9 lakh voters. “Following verification and disposal of applications (including Forms 7 and 8), around 2 lakh voters are expected to be added to the rolls,” he stated.Some 44% of Form 7 applications processed in Bengaluru during SIR have been accepted.Rao indicated the post-SIR rolls could be used for forthcoming GBA elections. “There is no need to panic if some names are missing. Election Commission will take steps to conduct a special drive to include all eligible voters in the list,” he added.EC, in a letter on Oct 9, issued guidelines on handling Form 7 applications. During SIR, the commission allowed booth-level agents (BLAs) to file applications in bulk, with a limit of 50 forms per day before publication of draft electoral rolls and 10 forms per day thereafter.For individual voters, online applications were limited to six at a time. articles.title: Ex-Saints RB Signs With Browns Amid Judkins, Sanders Injury Concern
articles.summary: The world of NFL running backs is always changing quickly. One RB who began his season with the New Orleans Saints is already onto his third team of the 2026...
articles.body:
The world of NFL running backs is always changing quickly.

One RB who began his season with the New Orleans Saints is already onto his third team of the 2026 campaign.

That'd be Audric Estime, who signed with the Cleveland Browns earlier this week.

Estime had been on the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad, so the Browns had to sign him onto their active roster in order to nab him from there.

And given the current injury state Cleveland is in, the Browns might actually need to use Estime in Week 6 against the Baltimore Ravens .

It's ironic, because the Saints have already found themselves with plenty of RB injury troubles of their own.

Estime was originally a fifth-round pick of the Denver Broncos in the 2024 NFL Draft out of Notre Dame.

He only lasted one season in Denver before being waived, and the Philadelphia Eagles had him for the first two months of the 2025 season.

They cut him, though, and Estime joined the Saints for the tail end of 2025. He got into seven games for New Orleans and ran 46 times for 198 yards and a touchdown to go with 12 catches for 103 yards.

That was enough to keep Estime around through this preseason, but the Saints waived him due to injury in mid-September.

The Vikings signed Estime to their practice squad about a week later. And it was two weeks after that the Browns claimed him.

So Estime had NFL action with the Broncos in 2024 and the Saints in 2025. He played for New Orleans in the preseason this year but has yet to get into an NFL regular season game in 2026.

The Browns are in dire need at the running back position right now.

They have already placed Raheim "Rocket" Sanders on injured reserve — and no, he's not related to Shedeur, but he was their RB2 in the early stages of this season.

And their starting running back, Quinshon Judkins, didn't practice on Wednesday. His status for Week 6 is in doubt.

If Judkins is out, the Browns are left with just Jaleel McLaughlin of the players who were previously on their team.

They have brought in Estime to potentially pair with McLaughlin in what would be a backfield featuring two former Broncos.

The Browns do have one RB on their practice squad, too — Jaret Patterson, the former University of Buffalo star who would likely be elevated for gameday if Judkins is unable to play.

But Estime is set to be active either way, it seems, because the Browns probably wouldn't have signed him into an active roster spot off the Vikings' practice squad if they didn't plan on using him in some form. At worst, he's some much-needed insurance for a banged-up Cleveland roster.

articles.title: Gophers O-Lineman Lands Big Spot on Mel Kiper’s Top-25 NFL Big Board
articles.summary: The Minnesota Gophers are sitting on a bye, but Mel Kiper Jr. just handed center Greg Johnson a major draft-season boost.
articles.body:
One week after taking the Little Brown Jug from Michigan, the Minnesota Gophers went to West Lafayette on Saturday and got run over 41-13 by Purdue . Now, Minnesota enters their bye week 4-2 overall and 2-1 in the Big Ten.

The time off could not have come at a better time, because PJ Fleck and his Gophers have wounds to lick both physically and mentally before they take to Huntington Bank Stadium next Saturday against the Iowa Hawkeyes.

Minnesota's problems come on both sides of the ball. Their defense has been a roller coaster. Minnesota held Washington to 40 rushing yards and Michigan to 180 total yards in back-to-back wins. In their two losses, the defense has struggled mightily.

Back in September, the Gophers let Mississippi State run for 252 yards during the Bulldogs' 38-13 win at Huntington Bank Stadium. Then over the weekend, Purdue piled up an astonishing 305 yards on the ground out in West Lafayette.

Minnesota offensive line could be better… but could be worse too

On offense, moving the chains has been a chore, mostly due to their struggles in the run game. The Gophers average only 96.4 rushing yards per game (3.6 YPC) . That ranks 120th in the country.

Pass protection, however, has been the bright spot for Minnesota's offense, allowing just four sacks on the season ( 0.8 per game ). That's tied for 12th nationally. That's an impressive feat, especially considering the Gophers are down their starting and backup centers on the o-line.

Dot by Drake Lindsey — Billy M (@BillyM_91) September 12, 2026

And that brings us to Greg Johnson, who might be the only reason the offensive line has shown any sign of life through six games and the main reason QB Drake Lindsey is still alive.

Pro Football Focus has Minnesota's senior interior o-lineman graded at 80.3 overall on offense this season. That ranks 13th among 737 FBS guards and fourth in the Big Ten.

On the year, Johnson has allowed only one QB pressure in 202 pass-blocking snaps, though PFF's grading system says that is his biggest weak spot (74.9). His 81.1 run-blocking grade ranks 11th nationally.

Greg Johnson leads Mel Kiper's interior offensive line rankings

Whatever it is Greg Johnson is selling, ESPN's NFL Draft superstar, Mel Kiper Jr., is buying it. On Thursday, Kiper released an updated 2027 NFL Draft Big Board .

In it, he crowned the 6-foot-6, 325-pound Prior Lake product as the No. 15 overall prospect in the 2027 class and the No. 1 overall interior offensive lineman.

15. Greg Johnson , G/C, Minnesota Height: 6-6 | Weight: 325 2026 stats over six games: Six starts, zero sacks allowed, one pressure allowed Johnson has played significant snaps at left guard and center this season, and he's a high-level blocker at both spots. Versatility is one of his best traits; he had 50-plus snaps at both tackle spots last season in addition to his work on the interior. Johnson is a strong run blocker, with an aggressive, nasty edge to his game. He's powerful and can sustain well. But he also anchors well in pass protection, and he has never allowed a sack across 43 career games (34 starts). Mel Kiper Jr., ESPN

2026 stats over six games: Six starts, zero sacks allowed, one pressure allowed

Johnson has played significant snaps at left guard and center this season, and he's a high-level blocker at both spots. Versatility is one of his best traits; he had 50-plus snaps at both tackle spots last season in addition to his work on the interior. Johnson is a strong run blocker, with an aggressive, nasty edge to his game. He's powerful and can sustain well. But he also anchors well in pass protection, and he has never allowed a sack across 43 career games (34 starts).

Kiper lists Johnson as a guard/center. He's the only Minnesota player listed anywhere in Kiper's article, which includes a top 25 big board and a top-five (plus honorable mentions) at every position.

Behind him among interior offensive linemen are Iowa's Kade Pieper (No. 19 overall), Notre Dame's Anthonie Knapp, Cincinnati's Evan Tengesdahl and Ohio State's Austin Siereveld. Pieper, a PFF first-team All-American in 2025, and his Hawkeyes will be in town next weekend.

PFF grades and watch lists back up the hype

Johnson moved to center for the win at Washington, and he has stayed there with starter Ashton Beers lost for the season . That's why he's logged only 197 snaps there, and 157 at left guard. In the end, it's a switch that could pay off in Johnson's favor because it's allowed him to prove the exact flexibility Kiper is talking about.

First start at center for Minnesota IOL Greg Johnson (6-6 1/2, 327) since 2024 and he was exceptional. Round 1 player. — Jordan Reid (@Jordan_Reid) September 28, 2026

Jordan Reid (@Jordan_Reid) September 28, 2026

His peak came in the 27-24 win at Washington, when PFF graded him 88.4 overall, the top mark among every guard in the country that week. The Football Writers Association of America named him Outland Trophy National Player of the Week , and on Tuesday he landed on the Lombardi Award 's midseason watch list of 60 players.

Johnson could end a long first-round drought

None of this came out of nowhere. Per his official bio , Johnson started all 13 games at center in 2024, then started 11 at left guard plus one each at left and right tackle in 2025. He was All-Big Ten honorable mention last season and Academic All-Big Ten in 2024 and 2025.

Love the downfield blocking by Greg Johnson (#65, the center) on this play — Thor Nystrom (@thorku) October 4, 2026

Love the downfield blocking by Greg Johnson (#65, the center) on this play

If he holds onto that ranking, Johnson would snap a long dry spell. The last Gophers offensive lineman drafted in the first round was center Brian Williams , No. 18 overall to the New York Giants in 1989.

After the bye, Minnesota hosts Pieper and the Hawkeyes on Oct. 24 at Huntington Bank Stadium. Pieper has been every bit as good as Johnson on PFF's charts.

He goes in with an 81.6 overall grade at right guard, which actually ranks two spots ahead of his Minnesota counterpart nationally. Also per PFF, Pieper has allowed two pressures and no sacks on the season.

Iowa is running the ball better than Minnesota, though not by a huge margin, at 148.4 yards per game and 4.9 yards per carry. Like the Gophers, Iowa is allowing just 0.8 sacks per game. Hawkeyes tackle Trevor Lauck also made Kiper's board at No. 23.

articles.title: ESPN’s Dan Orlovsky Urges Fans to Donate to GoFundMe to Support His Family Amid Brother-in-Law’s Death
articles.summary: ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky has revealed that his brother-in-law, Federico “Fed” Lascano, died unexpectedly, leaving behind his wife and three young sons. The...
articles.body:
ESPN analyst Dan Orlovsky has revealed that his brother-in-law, Federico "Fed" Lascano , died unexpectedly, leaving behind his wife and three young sons.

The former NFL quarterback, 43, shared the heartbreaking news on X on Thursday, October 15, explaining that his sister, Christine , is now facing the challenges of raising her children without her husband.

"This weekend, our family experienced an unimaginable tragedy," Orlovsky wrote, revealing that Lascano had died over the weekend.

The couple, who had been together since college, shared three sons: Brayden , 18, Cameron , 16, and Colton , 11.

Orlovsky explained that the sudden loss has left his sister confronting both emotional and financial uncertainty, prompting him to share a GoFundMe campaign to support the family.

"In the midst of trying to process this devastating loss, my sister is now facing the overwhelming reality of navigating life as a solo parent and a single-income household, all while helping her boys cope with the loss of their dad," he wrote.

According to the fundraiser, Lascano had been the family's primary financial provider, and donations will help Christine cover everyday expenses, including groceries, household bills and other necessities while she and her sons grieve.

Any remaining money will be placed in a fund to help with the boys' education and future essential expenses.

Orlovsky also urged those unable to contribute financially to share the fundraiser or keep his family in their thoughts.

"No family should have to face this kind of heartbreak, and no one should have to worry about how they will manage financially while trying to put the pieces of their lives back together," he wrote.

The cause of Lascano's death has not been publicly disclosed.

The announcement prompted an outpouring of condolences from across the football community, including former NFL quarterback Brian Hoyer , who wrote , "Sorry for your family's loss Dan."

NFL reporter Ed Werder also expressed his sympathy on X , encouraging others to support Christine and her sons during the difficult time.

Orlovsky, who played 12 seasons in the NFL before retiring in 2017, joined ESPN as an analyst in 2018 and has become a familiar face on programs including NFL Live , Get Up and First Take .

He concluded his message by thanking those who had rallied around his family.

"Our family is heartbroken, but we are so grateful for the love and support surrounding them during this unimaginable time," he wrote.

articles.title: Pat McAfee Addresses 'Monday Night Football' Rumors in Video Amid Troy Aikman's ESPN Contract Talks
articles.summary: Amid growing speculation about Troy Aikman's future as the color commentator for ESPN's Monday Night Football coverage, Pat McAfee is shutting down rumors that he is being eyed as a potential replacement.
articles.body:
Amid growing speculation about Troy Aikman's future as the color commentator for ESPN's Monday Night Football coverage, Pat McAfee is shutting down rumors that he is being eyed as a potential replacement.

On Thursday's episode of The Pat McAfee Show , McAfee said there has "never been a conversation" about him joining the Monday Night Football booth with Joe Buck.

Aikman is in the final season of his original contract with ESPN that was signed in 2022. The move maintained his partnership with Buck that began in 2002 when they both worked for Fox Sports.

Buck, who was also in the final year of his original ESPN deal, signed a six-year extension with the network last month that will pay him around $108 million.

It doesn't appear as if ESPN and Aikman will strike a deal anytime soon. The Dallas Cowboys legend told 96.7 The Ticket in Dallas (via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News ) he will be a free agent at the end of the season:

"There's probably a time and a place for all that. I don't know if now is the time. I don't know if it's hard to figure out kind of what happened. I'll broadcast through this season and I'll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens. I'm looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot may be."

Aikman's comments came on the heels of a report from Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports about "unspoken tension" between Aikman and Buck, leading to "an argument" between the two prior to the the Buffalo Bills-Los Angeles Rams game on Monday night.

The speculation about McAfee began on Monday when Michael McCarthy of Front Office Sports wrote a column suggesting that ESPN's planned Super Bowl 61 alt-cast led by McAfee could be a tryout for him to replace Aikman in the booth next season.

McAfee has an enormous presence on ESPN airwaves already between his podcast, analyst role on College Gameday , alt-casts during the College Football Playoff national championship and forthcoming Super Bowl alt-cast.

ESPN also announced McAfee will lead Monday Night Football alt-casts this season in games with the Manning-cast is not airing. The first game with McAfee's crew will be this coming week for the Washington Commanders-San Francisco 49ers matchup.

articles.title: Baker Mayfield injury update: Buccaneers QB’s status confirmed for Steelers game
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers face an important decision about Baker Mayfield ahead of their Week 6 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers head into their Week 6 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers facing an important question at quarterback.

Tampa Bay's quarterback, Baker Mayfield, has been sidelined due to an injury he suffered in Week 3. Amidst speculations about his potential return, the latest update clarifies the quarterback's status for Sunday.

Baker Mayfield is unlikely to return against the Pittsburgh Steelers

Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6). Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images.

Mayfield is working his way back from a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand, but he is not ready to return, (h/t Mike Garafolo of NFL Network).

Garafolo reported that Mayfield badly wants to play for the Buccaneers, although the likelihood is that he will miss another game.

The injury occurred during Tampa Bay's loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 27 and has kept Mayfield out of the team's subsequent matchups. He was also absent from the portion of Wednesday's practice open to the media, with the Buccaneers continuing to monitor his recovery.

Jalon Daniels set to start for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers against the Pittsburgh Steelers

With Mayfield unlikely to return, Jalon Daniels is expected to make his third consecutive start for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The undrafted rookie has taken over since Mayfield's injury, gaining valuable experience while the starter works toward a comeback.

Daniels comes into the matchup after leading Tampa Bay to a 24-16 victory over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5. He completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown without throwing an interception, adding 23 rushing yards. It was his first NFL win as a starting quarterback .

articles.title: Frank Reich on Jets RB room: ‘We have the best 1-2 combo in the NFL’
articles.summary: After Braelon Allen's career game against the Browns, OC Frank Reich declared the Jets running back has the best "one-two combo in the NFL."
articles.body:
Sunday's win against the Browns was a coming-out party for Jets running back Braelon Allen.

The third-year back had his best game as a pro, rushing for 116 yards on 24 carries and scoring a touchdown to help New York capture its second victory of the season. And that performance had OC Frank Reich gushing over the Jets' running back room, especially Allen, when speaking with the media Thursday.

"We have the best one-two combo in the NFL," Reich said. "Braelon is outstanding. Really smart. Has the explosive runs, that was the big thing last week. We had four explosives in the game, tied for the most in the year for us. And a lot of that was his running."

One of Allen's explosive runs was the game-winning score in the fourth quarter. With the Jets down 12-10, and in a third-and-nine situation on the Browns' 22-yard line, quarterback Geno Smith handed the ball to Allen, who scampered to the end zone relatively untouched.

Reich revealed that he actually called a pass on that play, but Smith checked it to a run after he recognized a hole in Cleveland's defense. And once Allen had the ball, the back did the rest with his ability.

"He's stereotyped as that big bruiser inside between the tackles. I don't see that at all," Reich said of Allen. "He's got good feet. He's a big man, but he's got quick feet. He's shifty, he's got good acceleration and good speed."

It's been tough sledding the first few seasons for Allen. In his rookie campaign, he rushed for 334 yards on 92 carries, while playing behind Breece Hall. Allen then suffered a knee injury that cut his 2025 season short after just four games. But this season, Allen is being used more and is already close to reaching career-highs in rushes and rushing yards.

A big part of that is Hall, the No. 1 in Reich's perceived combo, missed the last two games due to a quad injury and is still considered week-to-week ahead of the Jets' matchup with the Patriots. If that's the case, Allen will likely see the bulk of the carries, which Reich and the Jets are completely comfortable with.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts Out for Eagles vs. Panthers, Latest Details on Superficial Blood Clot Injury
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot.

The Eagles released a statement on the situation:

"On Thursday, October 8th, Jalen visited the training room after practice requesting treatment for his calf. He informed the medical staff he had been cleated during the Rams game on October 4th. This was his first treatment session for the calf injury following the game, after having practiced in full both Wednesday and Thursday. On Friday, Jalen received treatment, practiced in full, and was added to the practice report.

Tomlin's Take After Cowboys' Players-Only Meeting 💀

"Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team's flight to London and walkthrough. The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot. Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play. Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia.

"Jalen played without limitation in the game Sunday, received treatment on Monday and Tuesday, and practiced in full on Wednesday, as reflected in the practice report. Throughout our time in London and this week, we have remained in communication with the league office regarding the matter.

"On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority."

Hurts previously dealt with a calf injury that he suffered during a Week 4 matchup with the Los Angeles Rams, but was able to play through it in Philadelphia's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 5.

Availability hasn't been a major issue for Hurts throughout his career, as he appeared in 48 of a possible 51 games from 2023-25.

This season, the 28-year-old has completed 57.8 percent of his passes for 933 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions in five games/

Hurts has also continued to make plays with his legs, rushing for 107 yards and one touchdown.

Philadelphia (2-3) is looking to clinch its sixth consecutive playoff appearance and third straight division crown. After capturing a Super Bowl title during the 2024 season, the Eagles suffered a disappointing elimination in the Wild Card round last year.

With Hurts out, backup passer Tanner McKee will likely fill in.

articles.title: Cowboys DC Christian Parker Expects to Call Plays from Sideline Despite Jerry Jones' Comments
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker told reporters Thursday that he will "most likely" remain on the field calling plays amid the team's defensive struggles and owner Jerry Jones' recent comments that the DC would be heading to the booth.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker told reporters Thursday that he will "most likely" remain on the field calling plays amid the team's defensive struggles and owner Jerry Jones' recent comments that the DC would be heading to the booth.

Dallas has allowed an NFL-high 6.4 yards per play and sits at 2-3 after losing to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

On Tuesday, Jones said Parker's location would change as Dallas gets ready for a Sunday Night Football matchup at the Green Bay Packers.

Tomlin's Take After Cowboys' Players-Only Meeting 💀

"You search for what we can do differently that would give us better results," Jones told 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday (h/t Sean Leahy of Yahoo Sports).

"That's the main emphasis that we would spend some, let's say, specific attention to areas. We're going to coach the defense from not on the field, but up above. Parker's going up above.

"You should be looking for ways to adjust and make changes to improve. That's the point of improving from the results we had the last few weeks."

However, it appears that Parker will be staying on the sidelines.

The 34-year-old Parker has coached in the NFL for eight seasons after working the college ranks for six years. Before Dallas, Parker most recently served as the Eagles' defensive passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach in 2024 and 2025.

The Eagles won the Super Bowl to cap the 2024 season in part because of their tremendous pass defense, which shone in a 40-22 Super Bowl win over the Kansas City Chiefs.

Entering this season, Dallas gave up the second-most (and then the most) points allowed per game in 2024 and 2025, respectively. The Cowboys brought in Parker in hopes of turning the defense around (Dallas also made numerous investments in personnel this offseason, including drafting safety Caleb Downs, trading for linebacker Rashan Gary and signing Jalen Thompson).

However, Dallas is still struggling defensively. In Week 5, Dallas fell to Tampa Bay undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, who was making his second NFL start. An efficient Daniels looked calm, poised and collected en route to a 24-16 win, and Tampa Bay running back Bucky Irving rushed for 165 yards.

Now the Cowboys go to Green Bay to face a 3-2 Packers riding the high of a strong 31-7 win over their arch-rival Chicago Bears. It's a tough game on paper for a Dallas defense facing a previously struggling Packers offense that is figuring some things out (e.g. Green Bay amassed a season-high 428 yards).

Kickoff is set for 8:20 p.m. ET on Sunday.

articles.title: A.J. Brown Updates Status for Patriots vs. Jets, Return Timeline amid Ankle Injury Recovery
articles.summary: New England Patriots wideout A.J. Brown returned to practice this week, after being on injured reserve with an ankle injury, and updated reporters on his status ahead of Sunday's matchup with the New York Jets.
articles.body:
New England Patriots wideout A.J. Brown returned to practice this week, after being on injured reserve with an ankle injury, and updated reporters on his status ahead of Sunday's matchup with the New York Jets.

"I feel pretty good," he said Thursday. "It's one step at a time with me, each and every day, just trying to increase my [workload], and just see how I respond each and every day. But I feel good, on the grass, practicing, working on the sides a little more."

"He hasn't been out there for four weeks, so we'll get him out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple of days," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters Wednesday. "I think it's difficult sometimes to stay engaged, but I think his routine was really good, and his ability to be around the guys in the meetings and then also focus on his rehab and treat everything as a pro."

Brown, 29, was New England's major offseason acquisition, coming over in an offseason trade from the Philadelphia Eagles. But he suffered a high-ankle sprain in the team's Week 1 loss against the Seattle Seahawks and his 21-day practice window was opened this week.

Getting back the three-time Pro Bowler and one-time Super Bowl champion will obviously boost an offense that was already starting to find its groove again in recent weeks, although the timeline for Brown's return remains uncertain.

Another offseason addition, Romeo Doubs, has led the passing attack in Brown's absence. He's caught 13 passes for 219 yards and two scores. Drake Maye has also relied on Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and tight end Hunter Henry, and the Patriots have run the ball well.

But Brown provides a downfield threat and is one of the best contested-catch weapons in football. Upon his return, he'll immediately be the top priority in the passing game and should create opportunities for his teammates as well.

"I think you see it in the NBA," Maye told reporters. "It's probably the closest thing that I can think of. When they start doubling the best player once they get past half court, then they're just leaving a corner 3 open or leaving a guy open for a dunk. So, it's kind of like playing receiver and with a guy like that—we've got a lot of guys that have made plays now, so it's going to be tough on defenses."

articles.summary: Haley Cavinder revealed the smooth DM Jake Ferguson sent that sparked their romance, from a simple golf question to a Dallas Cowboys love story.
articles.body: Welcome to a Thursday in the middle of October. Or I should say, welcome to the latest edition of True Romance. Today is all about pushing back on the notion that romance has been defeated and it no longer exists. For those buying in on that, and I'm sure for some it's the case, I present to you several examples that, despite a possible downward trend overall, there are those making it work. If nothing else, there's hope. We have a full slate from the smooth athlete to influencer DM that landed to couple that pole dance together and even a couple of actors who covered their workplace in romance. Light a candle, relax and let’s get into it. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Long before the lucky pregame butt squeezes or the messages written on the back of Haley Cavinder's pants or even taking the heat for Jake Ferguson's bad game, there was the classic shooter taking his shot. The Dallas Cowboys tight end slid into the former college athlete and influencer's DMs with a line that ended up working and anyone can use. Haley said on an episode of People's WAG World, "He just DMed me and asked how my golf game was." And there's this idea floating out there that you can't meet people. Firing off a wild DM usually doesn’t work. A "How's your golf game" is smooth. The two hit it off, and now they're married, with a story to tell their grandkids one day. Grandpa was in the NFL and grandma used to dance on TikTok. They met after he sent her a message on social media. A love story as old as time. "I don’t like to get high or too low when it comes to that stuff. I wasn’t looking for anything, and I don’t know if Ferg was at that time either," she continued. "But then we spent 10 days together straight, and he’s just a good, down-to-earth human being." If you're having trouble finding someone, maybe you're just looking in the wrong places and sending DMs that aren't landing. There is hope. Fire off one about golf to a TikToker and see what ends up playing out. JOE BURROW'S GIRLFRIEND SHARES CHEATING HOT TAKE, WOMAN'S SISTER HOOKED UP WITH HER DATE & REGAINING THE SPARK Before we move on, let's find out the results of the poll from last week. The "Do you go through with the wedding if your husband-to-be calls you your sister's name at the altar?" one. In a stunner, given that the woman who this happened to did go through with the wedding, an overwhelming 72.5% said no, you leave that jerk at the altar. An unforgiving bunch of hopeless romantics, I suppose. Go follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook and keep sending your emails here: sean.joseph@outkick.com (anonymously if you prefer). Couples that pole dance together, stay together I bet, had that couple been pole dancing together, the husband-to-be wouldn’t have said the name of the bride's sister at the altar. Because if you didn’t already know, couples who pole dance together are weirdos. Let me finish. Weirdos who "strengthen their bonds and keep the spark alive." Take it from Los Angeles newlyweds Misha and Sam who, if they need pole dancing or anything as newlyweds to keep the spark alive, might be doomed. But that will be something they'll never be confronted with as long as they keep hopping on the pole together. And that's what we're here to focus on. The positive aspects of what these two are doing. Their first dance featured "saucy flips and splits on the polished pole," according to the NY Post. It turns out hitting the pole can be done in front of others. That's an interesting twist to this that I didn’t see coming. I was thinking this was more of an in the privacy of your own home activity. But why not something for everyone? Who needs movie nights or long walks when you have this and all of its options? "There’s a lot of stigma around pole dancing, some people might think, ‘Oh, that’s just for strippers,’" Misha told The Post. "Yes, it has sensual roots. But there’s so much athleticism that go into it. It’s a lot harder than it looks. We love it." Sam, who is the one who suggested they get into pole dancing, said, "A lot of people think pole is just for women. It’s strange for them to see a guy do it, especially with his [female] partner. I just don’t feed into the negativity." He added, "There are times I have to hold all of Misha’s weight while we’re doing a move, or she may have to position herself in a certain way to accommodate me. It’s like a metaphor for marriage." There really is something out there for everyone. If you're willing to take a chance, you could be one of those who finds the person you want to pole dance with for the rest of your life. That's a lovely thought, isn't it? If you think about it, pole dancing together really is just a metaphor for marriage. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER This Week In True Romance Follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook. Keri Russell and Matthew Rhys were 'having sex all the time' in their disguises on set of The Americans As much as I'd like to believe that couples pole dancing will work for people, and I'm sure it will for some, I can tell you a relationship built on having sex all over the set you're working on does work. At least it has for Keri Russell and Matthew Rhys. They've been together since late 2013 after starting their relationship while working on the series "The Americans". We now know that when they weren't filming they were busy on set having sex in their disguises. Why do we know that? Well, because it's 2026 and everyone tells everybody else everything. Which reminds me, I'll have to tell the story sometime of a graveyard at night and the back of a Nissan Pathfinder. Anyway, back to Keri and Matthew making a mess of their workplace. "We were falling in love and staying up all night and having sex all the time and just wearing disguises, like, I’m f---ing [in] crazy wigs and wearing pearls," Russell said during a podcast appearance, reports Entertainment Weekly. "When have you ever worn pearls and [been] f---ing in trailers and f---ing everywhere. I mean, it was insanity. It was so fun and sneaky, and sexy, and so good." If that doesn’t say true romance, I don't know what does. Congratulations to the happy couple for both their extracurricular activity on the set and for extending hope for others. Well done. What's the male equivalent of a woman wearing sexy underwear expecting them to be seen by her date? We've done a ton of these, and I don’t know that we've come across a more important question. She puts on her sexy underwear and he does what? If you were expecting a lot of effort here, you're going to be disappointed by the folks weighing in on Reddit, although something tells me that won't be a first. Sure, there are those who put in some work, but go ahead and set your expectations appropriately. Not that slipping on special underwear is a heavy lift. Some guys do that too. A blown out waistband could ruin the mood. On the other hand, a lovely Borat-style mankini could get the evening going. Song of the week - MP from Staunton, Virginia writes: Sean, this week’s True Romance column about the guy who boldly announced his love for his best friend’s girlfriend reminded me of a classic song by Ral Donner (that was originally recorded by Elvis). It’s called The Girl of My Best Friend. Unlike the guy in the column, the guy in the song had the good sense to keep his feelings to himself and just pine away for her. Hope this song is named Song of the Week. All the best. OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD ------------- We did it. We successfully made it through another week of romance. Let's do it again next Thursday before I log off for an entire week. Keep the song recommendations and anything else you want to share coming my way. If you were on the receiving end of a smooth DM, I want to know about it. As always, you can reach me, anonymously if you prefer, at sean.joseph@outkick.com. Go follow along on Twitter and Facebook.

articles.title: Eric Bieniemy Has 'No Problems' With Patrick Mahomes After Heated Exchange During Chiefs vs. Raiders
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy says there are no communication issues between himself and quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the wake of their heated exchange on the sideline of a Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy says there are no communication issues between himself and quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the wake of their heated exchange on the sideline of a Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

"I have no problems with guys venting their frustrations, because I want them to," Bieniemy told reporters Thursday. "That's part of the dynamic of the relationship that we have... if there's something that's taking place out on the field, they may have a better point of view than what we do from off the field, and so I want them to feel comfortable coming to share that stuff with me."

About his sideline conversation with Mahomes, Bieniemy said, "At that particular time, I'm pretty sure I had asked, 'Hey, man, what's going on? Is everything okay?'"

The Week 4 broadcast showed Mahomes speaking emphatically to Bieniemy after the Chiefs' final drive of the first half against the Raiders ended in a game-tying field goal rather than a go-ahead touchdown.

The Chiefs made the decision to go for the 28-yard field goal after Mahomes threw an incompletion toward tight end Noah Gray on third and goal.

"There's so many errors that take place throughout the case of a game, and hell, I've probably cussed somebody out about something," Bieniemy said Thursday. "But that stuff, it happens, and not that you ever take anything personally."

The Raiders went ahead just before halftime with a go-ahead field goal, although the Chiefs ultimately won after Kenneth Walker III took advantage of a fourth-quarter fumble to run in a game-winning touchdown.

The Chiefs could still look to finish off more scoring drives going forward. Kansas City is ranked 14th in the NFL with a 63 percent red-zone touchdown rate through Week 5.

This is not the first time Mahomes has drawn attention for an animated sideline discussion with Bieniemy, who rejoined the Chiefs for a second stint as offensive coordinator this offseason after previously serving in the role from 2018 to 2022.

Chiefs coach Andy Reid expressed faith in Bieniemy while speaking to reporters ahead of his team's upcoming Week 6 matchup against the visiting Los Angeles Chargers.

"I think EB is very thorough," Reid said. "He's demanding, and I appreciate that. As a head coach, I appreciate that, and the guys respond to it."

The victory over the Raiders allowed the Chiefs to head into their Week 5 bye as one of the three undefeated teams remaining in the NFL.

The Chiefs will look to ride the momentum of their 4-0 start into a game against the winless Chargers, which have recorded the NFL's second-fewest passing yards so far this season, when Sunday's game kicks off at 4:25 p.m. ET in Kansas City.

articles.title: Caleb Williams Injury Update, Bears QB Reveals Status for Falcons Game, Severity of Hamstring Tear
articles.summary: Caleb Williams doesn't know if he will be on the field for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
Caleb Williams doesn't know if he will be on the field for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.

"Before you start asking, (I) do not know if I'm playing yet," the Chicago Bears quarterback told reporters Thursday while revealing he still must undergo stress testing and pass medical protocols before he will be cleared to return.

Williams suffered a hamstring injury during Chicago's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. When he was carted off the field, Bears fans likely feared he would be lost for the season.

And while he seems to be approaching a much quicker return than that, Williams said he wasn't happy with the reporting and reaction to his setback he called a "hamstring tear" that was "pretty serious."

Williams' status is the biggest ongoing storyline surrounding the Bears.

He was listed as a full participant in practice for the second consecutive day on Thursday, suggesting he is nearing a return. What's more, he also changed his Instagram profile picture to a photo of John Wick with a bio that read, "I'm inevitable."

"He's doing a great job progressing and we'll see when we can make him available to help us win ball games," head coach Ben Johnson told reporters Monday. "But he's itching to get back as soon as he can, which is a good thing, and when we get the green light, we'll move forward from there."

Johnson also said he believed the Bears "have three guys that can win games in this league."

Chicago has done more than just tread water during Williams' absence, as Case Keenum led it to a 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent directed a 23-12 win over the New York Jets.

However, things took a turn last Sunday in a 31-7 blowout loss to the rival Green Bay Packers.

Bagent started the game but played so poorly at 12-of-21 for 87 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions that Johnson put Keenum into the game to finish. It was a reminder the Bears likely need Williams healthy and under center quickly if they are going to have any realistic chance of repeating as NFC North champions.

It seems like he isn't far away from returning, but he stressed he hasn't been fully cleared to play against the Falcons to this point.
